Increase the font scale if labels are hard to read. Check a tool screen and its dialogs after changing the scale to find a comfortable size.
Choose the app language independently of the font. If a selected font does not cover your language, try another font or the system option.
Tune transition speed, scrolling, and haptic strength
Layout and Vibration settings let you adjust how the interface moves and responds to touch.
Change Animation duration scale in Layout. Lower values shorten animations; higher values make transitions slower.
Try the available scrolling behaviors in Layout and choose the one that feels comfortable when browsing long lists.
Adjust vibration strength in Vibration. Reduce it or set it to zero if touch feedback is distracting.
Keep frequently used groups open in the regular settings layout
The regular settings layout can expand several groups at once. Settings categories instead open one section at a time, so group collapsing is not used in that mode.
For the fullscreen list, turn off Settings categories and enable Collapsible settings groups in Behavior. Use the arrow beside a group heading to expand or collapse it.
Long-press the group arrow in fullscreen settings to change its initial visibility. A toast confirms whether the group will start open or closed.
In the regular side panel, long-press a group heading to change its initial visibility. Searching still finds parameters inside collapsed groups.
Shape contrast, correct a color cast, and reuse curve presets

The horizontal axis is the original tone, from shadows to highlights. The vertical axis is the output tone. Raising a point brightens that range; lowering it darkens it. The straight diagonal leaves tones unchanged.
Start with the combined channel and a gentle S curve: lower shadows slightly and raise highlights to increase contrast.
Keep transitions smooth. Extreme bends can remove detail or create visible bands, especially in skies and gradients.
Switch to individual color channels to correct a cast. Compare neutral gray and skin tones before exporting.
One curve can be applied to several selected images. A shared curve gives consistent processing, but photographs with different exposure may still need individual corrections.
Select several images and switch between previews to check both the darkest and brightest example.
Export a curve preset as an .itcurve file and import it later to reuse the same control points.
Choose the output format and EXIF behavior, then save copies. Reset the curves if you want to start from the unchanged image.
Choose strips, grids, panorama, or screenshot stitching and control overlaps

Horizontal and vertical modes place images in a strip; grid modes make rows or columns. Panorama and Screenshot modes try to match overlapping content. Automatic matching needs shared detail between neighboring images.
Choose images in reading order and reorder them before fine tuning. For screenshots, keep a recognizable overlap between captures.
Use a strip or grid when exact order matters more than automatic alignment. Choose the scale direction and alignment to handle different sizes.
If automatic joining fails, remove an unrelated frame or choose a manual layout. Repeated patterns and moving subjects can confuse matching.
Positive spacing separates images; negative spacing overlaps them. Fading edges and blending affect an overlap, while the background fills uncovered areas.
Adjust horizontal and vertical spacing separately. Inspect seams at full size rather than relying only on the fitted preview.
Choose a solid background or gradient. Use a format with alpha support when uncovered areas must stay transparent.
Check output scale before saving: long strips and large grids can produce much larger images than any single source.
Arrange layers, choose a canvas, and combine opacity with blend modes

Image Stacking places several images on one canvas. Layer order, opacity, position, and blending determine how the result looks. It is useful for overlays, textures, double exposures, and compositing.
Add source images and reorder the stack. A fully opaque upper image can cover the images below it.
For each image, choose Fit, Fill, Crop, or another scale mode. Fit preserves the whole image; Crop fills the area by cutting off excess edges.
Adjust opacity and blending gradually. A blend mode changes how colors combine, so its effect depends on both layers.
Set the canvas size and position each layer. Save a PNG or another alpha-capable format when the canvas must remain transparent.
Combine a burst into exposure fusion, focus stacking, denoising, or light trails

Multi-frame Fusion combines 2–12 photographs of the same scene. Exposure mode balances differently exposed frames, Focus chooses sharp regions, Median suppresses changing details, and motion modes create long-exposure or trail effects.
Choose images with similar framing. Keep the camera steady; large viewpoint changes and parallax are difficult to align.
Enable alignment for small camera shifts. Crop to overlap removes borders that are not shared by all aligned frames.
Choose the mode for the source series: exposure brackets, shifted focus, a stable burst, or moving lights need different processing.

Controls depend on the mode. Exposure weights favor contrast, saturation, and well-exposed regions. Focus radius and strength control sharp-region selection. Trail controls govern which motion remains visible.
Change one parameter at a time and compare the same region. Strong settings can introduce halos or abrupt transitions.
Inspect moving subjects and fine edges for double contours. Remove an unsuitable frame if it makes the merged result worse.
Preview before saving the full result. For motion trails, keep the intended time order when reordering the series.
Rebuild a large picture from smaller images and balance detail against tile visibility

A photomosaic approximates the source picture with many small photographs. The source defines the overall composition; the tile collection supplies local colors and texture. A varied collection usually matches more regions well.
Choose the main image, then add tile images separately. Use tiles with varied brightness and color, rather than many near-identical pictures.
Increase columns for a more detailed overall picture. Fewer columns make individual tile photographs easier to recognize.
Tune repeat distance to avoid nearby repetition and color blending to pull tile colors toward the source. Strong blending reduces the original tile appearance.
Check both the full composition and zoomed-in tiles. Limit tile count while experimenting, then save the finished result at a useful viewing size.
Measure size, encoding time, SSIM, and PSNR on the same source
Compression Lab compares candidate formats on a selected reference image. Quality numbers are encoder-specific: JPEG 85 and another codec at 85 do not promise the same fidelity or file size.
Select source images, choose the reference, and enable the formats you want to compare. Run comparison after changing the selection or strategy.
Fixed quality uses the chosen encoder quality. Smallest at quality searches for a smaller file meeting the SSIM target. Best under size searches within the byte budget.
If a target cannot be reached, the result is marked accordingly. Lossless or fixed-setting encoders may not expose a useful quality range.

SSIM measures structural similarity and PSNR measures pixel error against the source. Larger values generally mean closer reconstruction, but neither score replaces looking at text, faces, gradients, or transparent edges.
Compare file size and encoding time alongside the metrics. Results from one photograph are not a universal ranking for every image.
Select a result and inspect the image itself. If the intended recipient does not support that format, choose a more compatible candidate.
Review the chosen result and selected sources before saving or sharing. Use Resize by file size when your main goal is a simple upload limit.
Add a background, breathing room, rounded corners, and a soft shadow

Screenshot Framing places an image on a decorative canvas. It is useful for release notes, portfolio examples, and tutorial illustrations. It adds presentation around the image rather than creating a real device mockup.
Pick a screenshot or photo and choose the canvas aspect ratio for its destination. Use padding to separate the image from the edges.
Choose a gradient preset or set the two colors yourself. Disable the gradient for a solid background.
Tune corner radius, shadow blur, and shadow opacity. Check that the shadow remains visible against the chosen background.
Read small interface text in the exported image. Decorative space can make the actual screenshot too small when a website scales the final card.
Control syntax, line wrapping, window decoration, and transparent export

Code Preview renders entered source text as a picture with syntax highlighting. It does not run the code. Choose a language explicitly so that keywords and punctuation receive appropriate highlighting.
Paste a focused example and choose the language and syntax theme. Remove private values from the text before sharing the image.
Set font size and line wrapping. Without wrapping, one long line can make the entire output unusually wide.
Toggle line numbers, file name, and decorative window buttons according to the context. These labels become part of the image.
Inner padding separates code from the window border; outer padding separates the window from the canvas. Window and canvas corner radii are independent.
Choose the background colors and adjust rotation or shadow only after the code is readable. Leave enough outer space for a rotated card.
Disable the canvas background for transparent output and choose an alpha-capable format such as PNG.
Check the exported picture at the intended display size. A short snippet with a larger font is often clearer than a whole file compressed into one card.
Understand formulas, zoom, iteration policies, coloring, and 3D cameras

A fractal image is calculated from a formula and its parameters. Changing the formula changes the underlying structure; changing a palette changes how calculated values are colored. Available controls depend on the formula.
Start with Mandelbrot or Julia. Move and zoom the preview to find a region, and reset the viewport to return to the starting view.
Increase iterations when detailed boundaries become flat or incomplete. Scaling or adaptive iteration policies can help as you zoom further.
Very deep zoom beyond 10¹²× requires Mandelbrot or Julia with power 2. Other formulas have different numerical limits.
Palette cycles and offset redistribute colors. Supersampling improves edge sampling but requires more work. For 3D formulas, camera yaw, pitch, and distance determine the view.
Change coloring and interior color after choosing the geometry. For attractors, sampling density can matter more than escape-time iteration settings.
For 3D scenes, inspect the camera and optional floor. Lighting and overlapping geometry can hide features even when the formula is correct.
Choose final output dimensions before saving. Large images with high iteration counts or supersampling can take substantially longer than the interactive preview.
Compare color models, mixing, related colors, shades, and distributions

Color Tools collects several views of the selected color: numeric information, mixing, harmonies, shades, and a histogram tool. A numeric color needs its color model to be meaningful; a HEX value is not an HSV triplet.
Choose the reference color and inspect its values. When copying a value elsewhere, check the expected model and whether alpha is included.
Use harmonies for related or contrasting colors and shades for lighter or darker variants. Judge the colors together on the intended background.
Pin the selected color if you want to keep it visible while scrolling through the tools. Use Pick color from image for a reference sampled from a photograph.
Export a palette as a PDF
Make a printable color sheet from an image or a palette file

Palette PDF turns extracted or imported colors into a document with swatches and optional labels. It is useful for discussing a color scheme or keeping a printable reference. Screen and printer output can differ.
Choose an image or a supported palette file. For an image, set the maximum number of extracted colors; a small count emphasizes dominant colors.
Set column count, margins, and spacing so that swatches and labels fit the page. Enable the source image only when it helps explain the palette.
Choose whether to show palette names, color names, HEX values, and the source file name. Save or share the finished PDF.
Create an animation, extract frames, merge GIFs, or convert to another animated format

GIF Tools separates extracting frames, creating GIF from images, merging animations, and conversion to JXL, APNG, or WebP. GIF has a limited palette, so photographs and smooth gradients may lose colors or show dithering.
Choose the operation first. When creating a GIF, order images as animation frames and set the frame timing.
Keep frame dimensions consistent when possible. Large frames and many frames increase memory use and output size.
Use extraction when you need still frames; use an animated conversion when you need to keep motion. Test playback in the destination app.
Build or split an animation while keeping smooth transparency

APNG stores animation with PNG-style color and transparency. It is useful for graphics with smooth alpha edges or colors that GIF cannot reproduce well, but its files can be large and support varies between apps.
Choose creation from images, extraction, merging, or conversion in APNG Tools. Set frame order before adjusting animation timing.
Preserve transparent source frames when alpha matters. Converting an already flattened JPEG cannot restore its missing transparency.
Preview the saved animation in the target app. A viewer without APNG support may display only a still frame.
Choose still conversion or frame-aware tools and check alpha and quality

For a single still image, ordinary format conversion is usually enough. WebP Tools is useful for creating, extracting, merging, or converting animated WebP. Lossy and lossless compression solve different size and fidelity goals.
Use an animation operation to preserve frames and timing. Opening an animation in a still-image workflow can leave you with one frame.
Check transparent borders against both light and dark backgrounds. Strong lossy compression can affect fine colored details even when alpha is present.
Test the result where it will be used. Some upload services recompress WebP or convert animated output to a still image.
JPEG XL and reversible JPEG packaging
Distinguish image encoding from JPEG reconstruction and animated conversions

Encoding pixels into JXL and packaging an existing JPEG for later reconstruction are different operations. Use JPEG to JXL and JXL to JPEG for the dedicated reconstruction workflow, rather than assuming any JXL can recover an original JPEG.
Choose JPEG to JXL for a compatible original JPEG that you want to package. Keep a source copy until you have checked the reverse operation.
Use Images to JXL for ordinary encoding and choose the available compression parameters for your fidelity and speed needs.
Use frame extraction, merging, or animated-format conversion for animated content. Test decoder support before sharing JXL with another app.
Map brightness to characters and control character density
ASCII Art replaces image regions with characters from a brightness gradient. The symbol sequence and font size affect the result: dense symbols represent different tones from spaces and small marks.
Choose an image with a clear silhouette or contrast. Tiny textures and busy backgrounds are harder to recognize as text.
Edit the character gradient and font size, then try inversion if light and dark areas appear reversed for your target background.
Copy or export the resulting text and use a monospaced font in the destination. Proportional fonts and changed line spacing can distort the picture.
Choose brush behavior, line width, colors, and readable marks

Drawing is useful for handwritten notes, marks, and highlighting image details. Brush mode, width, color, and zoom affect precision. The interface font setting does not control text rendered into an image.
Choose the drawing mode and start with a line width appropriate for the original image dimensions. Inspect the mark after zooming back out.
Use a color that remains distinguishable over both light and dark parts of the image. Avoid hiding the detail you are explaining.
Use undo while refining individual marks. For a reusable composition with editable text and layers, choose Markup Layers instead.
Choose output format and quality after editing. Default line width, color, path mode, magnifier, and orientation lock are available in drawing settings.
Remove image metadata in a batch
Clean embedded image information and verify the exported copies

Delete EXIF is intended for removing embedded metadata from selected images. Metadata cleanup is different from hiding visible information: a face, address, screenshot label, or filename can still reveal details.
Select the images to clean and review the batch before saving. Use Edit EXIF when you need to inspect or change particular fields instead.
Save cleaned copies and inspect an exported file in the metadata viewer. Supported metadata and container behavior differ between formats.
Check file names and visible content separately. Do not overwrite the only original if you may need its camera information later.
Use albums, previews, selection, and semantic search together

The built-in Gallery helps choose images for tools. Albums narrow the source set, while previews help check a picture before selecting it. Semantic search is optional and has its own preparation and category settings.
Open the relevant album before choosing a large batch. A selected album also matters when browsing semantic results and people groups.
Inspect similar-looking thumbnails in preview to avoid processing the wrong version. Check the selected count before sending images to a tool.
If a new file is missing, check its folder, media permissions, and whether the source app has finished saving it. A file picker can reach sources not shown in the media library.
Choose a container, compression method, password, and extraction options

Archive Tools supports packing selected files and extracting supported archives. Container format, compression method, and password protection are separate choices. A stronger compression level does not necessarily help already compressed photos or videos.
Choose the mode first. For creation, select the output format and available compression method; password support depends on that combination.
When extracting, inspect the archive contents and choose the extraction options and destination. Encrypted archives may request passwords individually.
If protection is unsupported or a password fails verification, resolve that before extraction. Keep the original archive until the extracted files have been checked.
Move between an image and its textual representation without confusing encoding with encryption
Base64 represents binary data using text characters. It is useful for data exchange and embedded images, but it increases the amount of data and does not protect the contents.
Choose image-to-Base64 to encode a source image, or Base64-to-image to decode supplied text. Make sure the complete value is copied.
Check whether the destination expects raw Base64 or a data URI containing a MIME prefix. Extra quotation marks or unrelated text can break decoding.
Preview the decoded image and save it as a file when practical. For private data, use actual file encryption rather than Base64.
Highlight visual changes and export a comparison report

Compare PDF highlights visual differences between two documents. It is useful for checking changed layouts, diagrams, and scanned pages. It compares appearance rather than explaining edits as a text editor would.
Select the two versions in the intended order and check that corresponding pages have comparable size and orientation.
Choose the available comparison settings and highlight color. Small shifts can produce many differences even when the wording is unchanged.
Export the PDF report and inspect highlighted areas. Use the original documents for decisions about meaning or omitted content.
Resize PDF pages to a paper format
Normalize page size while preserving readable content

Resize PDF Pages fits pages to a selected paper size. This is different from cropping away content or rasterizing pages into images. Mixed-size documents need particular attention to margins and orientation.
Choose the target page size and available fitting options. Check portrait and landscape examples before applying to the document.
Inspect small text and page edges in the result. Reducing a large technical drawing to a small page can make labels unreadable.
Save a copy and verify the page size in your viewer or print dialog. Keep the original if it is needed for a different paper size.
Clean private and active PDF data
Review document cleanup options before sharing a copy

Sanitize PDF removes selected kinds of private or potentially active document data. It does not automatically cover visible names, addresses, or confidential text on the page. Cleanup can also remove useful document features.
Review the cleanup switches instead of assuming every option is needed. Keep an original copy before removing metadata, attachments, scripts, or other selected data.
Save a cleaned copy and test links, forms, and any features you intended to retain.
Review visible page content separately. Removing metadata or annotations alone does not guarantee that confidential text has been removed.
Arrange photo thumbnails with useful captions across printable pages
A contact sheet puts several images on each PDF page. It is useful for reviewing a photo set, cataloging references, or selecting files by name. It trades image detail for a compact overview.
Select images and put them in the desired order. Choose a grid that leaves thumbnails large enough for your purpose.
Enable useful caption fields such as sequence number, file name, dimensions, or file size. Long captions need extra space.
Check page previews and print scale before exporting. Use Images to PDF when each image should have a larger dedicated page instead.
Change page appearance while retaining text and vector structure
PDF Dark Mode changes page appearance using PDF blending rather than rasterizing text and vectors. It is useful when you want to save a dark copy, not just change the viewer theme.
Choose a built-in theme or custom blend color. Inspect diagrams and photographs as well as ordinary text.
Test text selection and links in the saved document. Annotation and form appearance may vary between PDF viewers.
Keep a light original for printing or recipients who need the original appearance. A dark page background can be expensive to print.
Choose page rendering instead of extracting only embedded pictures

Rendering a PDF page produces an image of the whole page, including text and vectors. Extract Images retrieves embedded pictures instead and may omit text or page layout. These operations serve different tasks.
Choose the page range and output resolution. Higher resolution helps small text but increases memory use and file size.
Choose an image format for the intended use. PNG suits crisp diagrams and text; a lossy format may be smaller for photo-heavy pages.
Inspect a rendered page at actual size before processing a large document. Rendered images no longer have selectable PDF text.
Pixel dimensions determine the actual image size. A percentage scales the source dimensions; a DPI value describes print density and is not a substitute for adding image detail.
Keep proportions when a stretched result would distort faces or objects. Use a crop or fitting mode when both target dimensions must be exact.
Preview the smallest text and finest edges. Sharpening cannot fully restore information removed by a large reduction.
Return to the original for a new export instead of repeatedly editing a lossy copy. Check save, overwrite, deletion, and metadata settings for a batch.
When the byte target is difficult
A file-size limit depends on format, dimensions, detail, and metadata. Quality alone may not reach a very small target, especially for noisy photographs or already compact files.
Choose the format supported by the upload destination. A smaller format is not useful if the receiving service cannot decode it.
Reduce dimensions when quality must otherwise fall too far. Compare text and faces after the reduction.
Check the saved file size and upload requirements. Some limits refer to pixels, not bytes, or include a separate dimension cap.
Order, masks, and a reproducible result
Filters are applied as a sequence. Blur before sharpening and sharpening before blur produce different images; strong contrast can also change the behavior of later effects.
Build corrections in small steps and reorder them when an effect looks unexpectedly strong. Disable or remove a filter to identify its contribution.
Use masks when an adjustment should affect only part of the image. Inspect mask edges for halos or abrupt transitions.
For a batch, inspect several source images rather than only the first one. The same parameters can clip highlights on a brighter photograph.
A crop removes unwanted borders; straightening corrects a tilted horizon; perspective correction changes a skewed quadrilateral into a more regular shape. Perspective transformations resample pixels.
Straighten before making a tight final crop, because rotating an image can introduce empty corners.
For documents, place free corners on the actual paper boundary. A bad corner estimate can stretch text unevenly.
Inspect the final edges and output dimensions. Cropping is not a way to increase the original resolution.

Automatic removal estimates the subject; manual erase and restore refine the mask. Transparent areas still need an output format that can store alpha. A checkerboard in the preview represents transparency, not a printed background.
Inspect hair, glass, gaps between fingers, and semi-transparent edges. Work at a useful zoom without judging only an enlarged fragment.
Alternate erase and restore instead of repeatedly expanding a rough edge. Check the result against contrasting backgrounds.
Reopen the saved file to confirm transparency. If an opaque format or alpha background setting fills it, exporting the same file again cannot recover the mask.
A markup project retains the composition for later editing, while a rendered image records the visible result. Keeping both makes later text or layout changes much easier.
Arrange layers intentionally and check the selected layer before changing position, size, or text. Higher layers can hide content below.
Keep required source assets available and save the editable project before making a flattened export.
Inspect the exported image at the intended size. A screenshot of the editor is not equivalent to rendering the composition.
OCR converts visible letter shapes into text. It can confuse similar symbols, lose punctuation, or merge columns. The selected language data and image preparation affect the result.
Choose the languages present on the page. Extra unrelated language data does not automatically improve recognition.
Crop unrelated areas, straighten the page, and avoid clipped highlights. Strong sharpening or thresholding can erase thin letter strokes.
Proofread names, numbers, and line breaks before copying or exporting. A searchable PDF may contain recognition errors even when its visible page looks correct.
SVG describes shapes rather than a fixed pixel grid. Converting a photograph into vectors approximates its appearance; it does not recover an original vector drawing or guarantee a smaller file.
Start with a clear silhouette, logo, or limited-color graphic when you want clean shapes. Photographic texture can generate many small paths.
Balance detail against simplicity in the available conversion controls. Inspect thin lines and small holes at several zoom levels.
Open the exported SVG in its intended viewer or editor. Compare transparency, gradients, and overall proportions before reuse.
Plan the page layout before export
The image sequence becomes document order. Page size, margins, and image fitting decide how much space each picture occupies; they do not add detail to a low-resolution source.
Reorder and rotate sources before exporting. Check mixed portrait and landscape pages for unexpected scaling or empty margins.
Use a lossless or high-quality source for small text and diagrams. Aggressive image compression can make a PDF compact but hard to read.
Open the finished document and verify page count, order, and readability. Use OCR or searchable PDF tools when selectable text is required.

Merge, Split, Rearrange, Remove Pages and Rotate change document structure. Split saves selected pages into one PDF; PDF to ZIP creates successive parts. Crop changes the visible page area but does not securely delete hidden content. Add page numbers after the final ordering.
Check whether a page selector refers to document page positions or printed page labels. A cover can make those numbers differ.
Preview the first, last, and boundary pages after splitting or merging. Keep a copy of the source document until the output is verified.
Apply page numbers after the final ordering and inspect the placement on pages with different sizes.

Protect PDF creates a password-protected copy; this screen does not expose separate printing or copying permission controls. Signature PDF places a visible image and does not create a certificate-based digital signature.
Choose protection appropriate for the recipient and store the password separately from the exported file.
Use Unlock with the required password. Removing restrictions or modifying pages can affect signatures already present in the document.
Test the saved copy in a PDF viewer before sharing it. Keep a source copy when the document may need later editing.
A naming pattern combines the enabled name parts. A filename extension should describe the actual encoded format; changing the extension alone does not convert image data.
Check a name preview after changing prefix, suffix, original name, timestamp, sequence number, or pattern.
Ensure repeated exports have distinct names unless overwriting is intentional. A checksum name can identify content, while a random name serves a different purpose.
Confirm the destination and overwrite settings before a large batch. A convenient name pattern should not replace checking which files will be written.
Decoded images can occupy far more memory than their compressed file size. Several layers, animation frames, or full-resolution intermediate results multiply that cost.
Start with a smaller representative batch and a modest output size. Increase size after checking the processing and result.
For a failed operation, reduce dimensions, frame count, or layer count before lowering output quality alone. Quality mainly changes encoding, not the decoded image size.
Keep enough free storage for temporary and output files. If the problem repeats on a small input, report the tool, parameters, format, and app logs.

AI Tools can estimate depth with a downloaded depth model or use a custom depth map. Depth describes distance, not a selection of a named object. Different result modes expose different controls.
Select your images and a depth model in AI Tools. Download the model if needed; optionally select a custom depth map.
Choose the depth result. Depth blur offers blur strength, focus depth and focus range; a depth mask or cutout offers focus and focus range.
Generate a preview, compare it with the original, and adjust the effect before saving. Use the depth map result when you need the map itself.
Reduce the size of images inside a PDF
Compress PDF recompresses embedded images at the selected quality. It uses a quality control rather than a target size in KB; documents with few images may shrink less.
Open Compress PDF and select the PDF. If it is protected, enter its password when requested.
Adjust Quality. Lower quality can reduce image size but may make text inside scanned pages harder to read.
Save or share the processed PDF and inspect a page with small text or detailed images.
Remove chosen annotation types from selected pages
Remove annotations can remove links, comments, highlights, shapes and form fields. Page selection and annotation types determine what is removed; it does not erase arbitrary printed text.
Open Remove annotations and choose the PDF. Select the pages to process.
Select the annotation types to remove. At least one type must be selected to save.
Check the preview and save a copy. Verify links or form fields you intended to keep in the saved document.
Inspect, change or remove individual metadata tags
Edit EXIF opens the selected image metadata for individual changes. Editing is available only when the image format supports writing metadata; the screen shows a warning for unsupported formats.
Select an image and open Edit EXIF to view its tags.
Update or remove individual tags in the metadata sheet. Clear all metadata only if you intend to remove every tag.
Close the sheet and save the result. Reopen the saved image to check the tags you changed.
Set the cache threshold and check interval
Automatic cache cleanup uses both a size limit and an interval. The limit and interval controls are enabled only when automatic cache clearing is enabled.
In Settings, enable automatic cache clearing before changing Cache limit or Cleanup interval.
Choose Cache limit from the provided sizes, from 20 MB to 2 GB.
Open Cleanup interval and choose On app launch, 1 day, 1 week or 1 month.
Merge combines complete PDF files in the order shown. It is useful for assembling a cover, report and appendices without turning pages into image files.
Select the PDFs, add missing files and reorder the list before saving. Remove an unwanted file from the list rather than leaving it in the output.
Save or share the combined PDF. Check the last page of each part and the first page of the next one.
If only certain pages are needed, first create a selection with Split PDF; merge those results. Add page numbers after the final order is settled.
Split PDF copies the selected pages into one new PDF. This operation is different from exporting page images or making a ZIP containing separate PDF parts.
Open a PDF and select the pages to keep using the page selector.
Preview the selection and save or share the new PDF. Check that the needed cover and attachments are included.
Use PDF to ZIP for successive groups of pages, or Extract pages for image output.
The selected pages are deleted from a saved copy. Use this for blank scans, duplicates or pages that should not be shared; at least one page must remain.
Select the pages to delete in the thumbnail grid. Here the selection means remove, not keep.
Check the neighboring pages so a double-sided scan does not lose the wrong side.
Save the copy and reopen it to verify the page count and order.
Rearrange changes page order inside one PDF. It is useful when scans were imported out of sequence or an appendix belongs in the middle of a document.
Open the PDF and drag page thumbnails into the required order.
Use visible page content to check the order: printed page numbers may differ from positions in the file.
Save the reordered copy, then add new page numbers if needed.
Rotate corrects page orientation in 90-degree steps. The automatic option aligns stored rotation values to the most common orientation; it does not recognize the direction of printed text.
Rotate individual thumbnails when only some scans are sideways; use Rotate all when the whole document needs the same turn.
Try automatic rotation for inconsistent page orientation metadata, then inspect pages containing text or diagrams.
Reset rotations if the result is wrong and save after checking both portrait and landscape pages.
Cropping changes the visible page rectangle. It can hide scan borders, but it does not securely erase content outside that rectangle from the PDF.
Select the pages to crop and adjust the horizontal and vertical ranges in the preview.
Inspect pages with different layouts before applying one rectangle to a group. Save a crop preset when the same margins recur.
Save a copy and check that headers, footers and page numbers remain visible. Do not use cropping to redact confidential information.
The numbering tool adds visible labels. The label format supports {n} for the current page and {total} for the total number of pages.
Finish merging, deleting and rearranging pages before adding numbers.
Edit the label format, for example {n} / {total}, and choose position, text size and color.
Inspect the preview on pages with different sizes. Save when numbers do not cover document content.
A PDF watermark places repeated text on selected pages. It identifies a copy but does not restrict copying, printing or editing.
Enter the watermark text and choose the pages that need the mark.
Set angle, size, color and opacity while inspecting the page preview.
Keep the document readable and save a separate copy for distribution.
This tool places a drawn or selected signature image on PDF pages. It does not create a certificate-based digital signature or verify the signer.
Create or choose a signature in the signature selector; saved signatures can be reused.
Choose pages and adjust horizontal offset, vertical offset, size and opacity.
Check alignment with the signature line in the preview before saving. Keep the unsigned source for later edits.
Protect PDF asks for a password and writes a protected copy. The screen does not offer a separate permission matrix for printing or copying.
Open the source PDF and enter a password, or use the random-password control.
Keep the password separately before saving; retain an unprotected source copy if it will need editing.
Open the saved PDF to verify the password and send it separately from the file.
Unlock creates a copy that no longer asks for the PDF password. It requires access to the document; it is not a password-recovery tool.
Select the protected PDF and enter the required password when prompted.
Wait for the unlocked confirmation, then save or share the result.
Reopen the saved copy to verify it no longer requests a password. Keep the protected original if it is still needed.
Grayscale PDF processes document images. It is useful for scans and printing, but should not be treated as a guarantee that every colored vector or text object becomes gray.
Open the PDF containing color scans or images.
Save or share the grayscale copy, keeping the color source when color carries meaning.
Check charts, stamps and small text in the output; colors that differed strongly may become similar gray tones.
Repair rebuilds PDF cross-reference information and writes the document again. It can help with structural damage but cannot recreate missing page data or recover a password.
Select the damaged PDF and work with a copy of the original.
Save the rebuilt result if the document can be processed.
Open it and inspect all important pages. A successfully written file is not proof that every original object survived.
Flatten renders each PDF page and builds a new image-based PDF. This stabilizes its visible appearance, but selectable text, editable objects and interactive elements are not retained as such.
Keep the original PDF if you need searchable text, forms or editable content later.
Adjust quality: a higher value increases rendering resolution and can produce larger files.
Save the flattened copy and zoom in on small text and lines. Use searchable-PDF OCR separately if a new text layer is required.
PDF to ZIP splits successive pages into PDF files and packs the results into one archive. The interval is the number of pages in each part, not an image export setting.
Open the PDF and choose the interval. Use 1 for one PDF per page.
Save or share the ZIP. A final part may contain fewer pages if the total is not divisible by the interval.
Extract the archive to check the parts. Use Split PDF for one arbitrary selection instead.
Comic conversion reads page images from CBR, CBZ, CB7 or CBT archives. Reading direction matters when a landscape spread is split into two pages.
Choose the archive and enter its password if required. Set page size or keep Auto.
Enable Split wide pages for two-page spreads and choose left-to-right or right-to-left reading.
Use Reverse page order or Skip cover only when appropriate for this archive. Save and check the first pages and a split spread.
Print PDF builds a new layout with one or more source pages on each sheet. It renders pages as images, so output quality affects both readability and file size.
Choose pages per sheet, paper size and orientation. More pages per sheet make each page smaller.
Set margins and quality, then inspect small text in the preview.
Save or share the prepared PDF and check it before printing. Keep the original if selectable text is needed.
Preview lets you inspect a PDF before choosing an operation. Text search depends on a text layer; a page that is only a scan may look readable but have nothing to search.
Open the PDF and inspect page orientation, margins and fine details.
Use the search field for documents containing text. Check spelling if no result is found.
For scanned pages without a text layer, use PDF OCR for text output or a searchable-PDF workflow before relying on search.
The normal PDF-to-text action extracts an existing text layer into a text file. Deep OCR renders the pages and opens batch text recognition for image-only scans.
Try normal text extraction on a digitally created PDF; save or share the resulting text.
If the PDF contains only page images, choose Deep OCR and configure the recognition engine and languages in the opened tool.
Proofread reading order, columns and numbers. Text extraction does not create a searchable PDF; use that separate OCR mode when required.
Frame extraction saves still images from a GIF file. Use it for an individual animation frame or a frame sequence; the exported images do not contain playback timing.
Open the GIF file and select all frames or only the required frame positions.
Choose the image format and its available quality options. Use a format with alpha, such as PNG, when transparent edges matter.
Save or share the selected frames and check their order. To keep motion in one file, use animated-format conversion instead.

GIF uses a limited color palette. Change FPS (frames per second) to change the delay between frames: higher FPS means a shorter delay. Extra crossfade frames smooth transitions and increase the frame count.
Select images, then reorder, add or remove them in the frame carousel.

Set output dimensions or use the first frame’s size. Set FPS, repeat count and quality. If earlier images remain visible behind later ones, enable Don’t stack frames; add crossfade frames only when a blended transition is wanted.
Save and play the result in its destination app; large dimensions and many frames increase memory use.
Merging appends complete animation clips into a single GIF. Clip order, reverse playback and boomerang are set before export; this does not place animations side by side.
Choose at least two GIF files and arrange them in the clip list. Set Reverse or Boomerang for individual clips when needed.
Normalize frame size to fit clips to the largest dimensions, or turn normalization off to keep original scale. Set the pause between clips and repeat count.
Save the animation and check each join: a pause, reversed clip or extra return sequence changes the overall duration.
APNG stores full-color animated frames with alpha. Converting to it preserves the available decoded pixels but cannot restore colors or transparency already lost in the source.
Choose the dedicated GIF to APNG mode and add the source animations. Several selected files are conversions, not a merge.
Save the conversion, then compare playback and file size. This conversion screen does not require a new FPS setting.
Open the saved APNG in the app where it will be used and check that motion, transparency and clip length are acceptable.
Animated WebP can reduce the size of animation, but this conversion encodes frames again. Inspect the result rather than assuming identical pixels or a smaller file.
Choose the dedicated GIF to WebP mode and add the source animations. Several selected files are conversions, not a merge.
Adjust WebP quality, then compare fine text, gradients and transparency against the source.
Open the saved WebP in the app where it will be used and check that motion, transparency and clip length are acceptable.
Animated JXL is useful when the receiving app supports it. This operation converts decoded frames and does not create a reconstructable original JPEG.
Choose the dedicated GIF to JXL mode and add the source animations. Several selected files are conversions, not a merge.
Adjust the JXL encoding parameters shown in the quality selector. Compare detail and output size after conversion.
Open the saved JXL in the app where it will be used and check that motion, transparency and clip length are acceptable.

Open the APNG file and select all frames or only the required frame positions.
Choose the image format and its available quality options. Use a format with alpha, such as PNG, when transparent edges matter.
Save or share the selected frames and check their order. To keep motion in one file, use animated-format conversion instead.
APNG keeps full-color frames and transparency. Compression effort changes encoding time and file size; it is not a lossy image-quality slider.
Select images, then reorder, add or remove them in the frame carousel.
Set output dimensions or use the first frame’s size. Set frame delay and repeat count. Increase compression effort when a smaller file matters more than export speed.
Save and play the result in its destination app; large dimensions and many frames increase memory use.

Adjust GIF quality and inspect fine details; if transparency or color is damaged, keep a full-color animated format.
Open the saved GIF in the app where it will be used and check that motion, transparency and clip length are acceptable.

JPEG to JXL uses the dedicated JPEG reconstruction path. It packages an existing JPEG without choosing a new pixel-encoding quality; this differs from Images to JXL.
Choose JPEG to JXL and select JPEG source files.
Save the JXL outputs and keep the original JPEGs until the reverse operation has been checked.
Use JXL to JPEG on a result to reconstruct it. For ordinary image encoding or animation, use Images to JXL instead.
JXL to JPEG requires JPEG reconstruction data inside the JXL file. A JXL created from arbitrary pixels or an animation does not necessarily contain that data.
Choose JXL files produced by a compatible JPEG-to-JXL reconstruction workflow.
Save the reconstructed JPEGs and verify them before deleting the JXL sources.
If reconstruction is unavailable, extract images from JXL and encode them as JPEG instead; that is a new lossy encoding, not restoration of the original file.
The whole-image filter mode applies one ordered stack to the selected images. A filter template can repeat a useful look, but the same values can affect bright and dark images differently.
Select one or more images and add filters individually. Adjust each filter while watching the preview and histogram.
Reorder filters when needed; order changes the result. Save or load a filter template for repeated processing.
Inspect several images from a batch, choose output settings and save. Use mask filtering when only a local area should change.
Mask filtering applies a filter stack to a drawn area of one image. Inverting the mask changes which side of the boundary receives the effect.
Open an image, add a mask and draw the area that needs adjustment. Undo or redo strokes when correcting the boundary.
Add filters to the mask and adjust their order and values. Switch the mask preview to inspect coverage; invert the mask if the surrounding area should be affected.
Check edges at a useful zoom before confirming the mask. Save the finished image after checking how multiple masks combine.

Text extraction shows recognition results for an image. Tesseract and PaddleOCR use different models; selecting the right language or model and preparing readable pixels matters more than using every option at once.
Choose an image or use the camera, then crop unnecessary background and straighten the text.
Select the recognition provider and its language data or model. Download missing data before working offline; use the available recognition settings for that provider.
Run recognition and proofread numbers, names and line breaks before copying or sharing the text.
Write to file processes multiple images and combines recognized text into one text document. It is useful for a set of scanned pages, but the output does not preserve the original page layout.
Choose the page images and check the list before processing. Remove files that should not contribute to the text.
Choose the OCR provider and its required languages or model, then download missing data if requested.
Save or share the combined text file. Check page order, repeated headers, numbers and recognition mistakes in a text editor.

Write to metadata stores recognized text in the image UserComment metadata tag. It does not draw text over the image or create a searchable PDF; metadata support depends on the image format and receiving app.
Choose the images and configure OCR language or model for their visible text.
Save the processed copies, then inspect UserComment with the metadata editor to confirm the text was written.
Use a text file for easy text exchange, or searchable PDF for document search. Remember that clearing metadata later also removes this text.
Open the author card for the project’s contact information.
Open Settings → Contact me → Author to show the card.
Choose the contact method in the card; opening it does not send a message automatically.
Share the app log file when a reproducible failure needs investigation.
Reproduce the problem, then open Settings → Contact me → Send Logs.
Wait for the file to be prepared and choose a destination in Android’s share sheet. Include the actions that caused the problem in your report.
The donation sheet offers ways to support development; it does not unlock editing tools.
Open Donation in the Contact me group.
Choose a method shown in the sheet and complete any payment in the service it opens.
Wallpaper-based colors replace the manually selected app palette.
Turn on Dynamic colors to use the system wallpaper palette.
Turn it off before changing Color scheme or enabling Allow image monet; those controls are disabled while dynamic colors are active.
AMOLED mode makes app surfaces black in the dark theme without changing exported images.
Choose a dark Night Mode, or use the system theme while Android is dark.
Enable AMOLED mode and inspect backgrounds; turn it off if you prefer the normal tinted dark surfaces.
Icon containers can be customized separately from the shapes of cards and buttons.
Open Icon Shape and choose a container in its preview sheet.
Adjust the available icon/container options there; use Shapes Type for the rest of the interface.
This option recolors the interface from an image selected for editing. It does not recolor that image.
Disable Dynamic colors first, then enable Allow image monet.
Open an image in an editor to use its palette; turn the option off for a stable interface palette across photos.
Borders and shadows are alternative ways to separate interface elements.
Move Border thickness from zero to add outlines, up to the displayed 1.5 dp limit.
Set it back to zero to enable the Shadows group; individual shadow switches are unavailable when borders are used.
The main screen title can be replaced with your own text.
Open Main Screen Title, edit the text, and confirm the dialog.
Check the result on the home screen; this changes the in-app heading, not output filenames or the launcher app name.
Choose the appearance of on/off controls without changing the settings they control.
Open Switch Type and select a style in the sheet.
Compare its checked and unchecked appearance on a nearby setting and choose the clearest style.
Slider style changes the interface used to adjust numerical values.
Open Slider Type and select one of the displayed styles.
Try a nearby slider to check its thumb and track; the style does not change numerical ranges.
The shape family controls the outlines of app surfaces and controls.
Open Shapes Type and choose a shape family from the sheet.
Use Corners Size to tune its strength after selecting the family; the existing strength is retained when you switch families.
Corner strength adjusts the selected interface shape rather than the image’s corners.
Choose Shapes Type first, then move Corners Size in its 0–2 range.
Inspect cards and buttons to find a comfortable outline; use an image-editing tool to round an exported image.
The throttle changes how quickly interaction-driven shape changes can repeat.
Adjust Corners Animation Throttle from 0 to 500 ms.
Try repeated taps on controls: increase the interval if shape changes feel too frequent, or reduce it for quicker reactions.
Fling behavior controls how lists continue moving after a swipe.
Open Fling Type and choose one of the available behaviors.
Swipe a long list to compare stopping behavior; select a calmer option if reaching a precise row is difficult.
The width slider changes the handle used by draggable sheets.
Move Drag Handle Width between 0 and 128 dp.
Open an option sheet to inspect the result; use Sheet gestures separately to allow or prevent dragging.
Dialogs can be placed where they are easier to reach on your screen.
Open Dialog Position and select a position in the preview dialog.
Open another dialog to check the placement, especially after rotating the screen.
This option centers dialog action buttons where the dialog layout supports it.
Enable Center Dialog Buttons and open a confirmation dialog to inspect the result.
Disable it to restore the usual alignment; the actions themselves are unchanged.
Choose the horizontal placement of floating action buttons used by tool screens.
Select an alignment in FAB alignment.
Open a tool with a floating save or action button and check that it is comfortable to reach.
Night Mode chooses whether the interface follows Android or uses a fixed light/dark theme.
Choose the light, dark, or system option in the Night Mode group.
Use AMOLED mode separately if you want black surfaces in the dark theme. Neither setting changes exported colors.
Turn off Containers in Settings → Shadows to remove shadows from containers and cards. This switch is independent of the other five shadow controls.
Open Shadows and turn Containers off. Turn it back on if you want those shadows again.
If this section is hidden or disabled, set Border thickness to 0 to access the controls. To disable all interface shadows, turn off all six switches in this section.
Turn off App bars in Settings → Shadows to remove shadows from app bars. This switch is independent of the other five shadow controls.
Open Shadows and turn App bars off. Turn it back on if you want those shadows again.
If this section is hidden or disabled, set Border thickness to 0 to access the controls. To disable all interface shadows, turn off all six switches in this section.
Turn off Buttons in Settings → Shadows to remove shadows from buttons. This switch is independent of the other five shadow controls.
Open Shadows and turn Buttons off. Turn it back on if you want those shadows again.
If this section is hidden or disabled, set Border thickness to 0 to access the controls. To disable all interface shadows, turn off all six switches in this section.
Turn off FABs in Settings → Shadows to remove shadows from floating action buttons. This switch is independent of the other five shadow controls.
Open Shadows and turn FABs off. Turn it back on if you want those shadows again.
If this section is hidden or disabled, set Border thickness to 0 to access the controls. To disable all interface shadows, turn off all six switches in this section.
Turn off Switches in Settings → Shadows to remove shadows from switches. This switch is independent of the other five shadow controls.
Open Shadows and turn Switches off. Turn it back on if you want those shadows again.
If this section is hidden or disabled, set Border thickness to 0 to access the controls. To disable all interface shadows, turn off all six switches in this section.
Turn off Sliders in Settings → Shadows to remove shadows from sliders. This switch is independent of the other five shadow controls.
Open Shadows and turn Sliders off. Turn it back on if you want those shadows again.
If this section is hidden or disabled, set Border thickness to 0 to access the controls. To disable all interface shadows, turn off all six switches in this section.
The language picker changes app text, not the contents of files you edit.
Open Language. On Android 13 and newer this opens the system app-language page when available; otherwise use the embedded language list.
Choose a language or the system/default option and return to the app to check translated labels.
Font scale controls app text size; the Default position uses the system scale.
Move the slider to a custom size or back to Default at the far left. Releasing it applies the change and recreates the screen.
Large values above 1.2 can crowd controls; check dialogs and small-screen layouts before keeping them.
Recent tools provide quick access to tools you have already opened.
Enable Show Recent Tools and use a few tools to populate the home-screen history.
Disable it to hide that section; use favorites for a manually chosen permanent list.
Tool search helps find a screen by its name without changing the home-screen order.
Enable Search in Tools arrangement, then return to the main screen and enter a tool name.
Disable it if you prefer browsing the list or category tabs; the tools remain available.
The Help & Tips button opens help from the main screen toolbar. It is shown by default.
Open Settings → Tools arrangement and turn Help & Tips button off to hide it, or on to show it again.
When the button is hidden, you can still open Help & Tips from settings.
Grouped mode organizes tools into type-based tabs instead of a custom order.
Enable Group tools by type and browse the main-screen tabs.
Disable grouping before editing Order; the order editor is unavailable while grouping is active.
Favorites can appear as their own tab alongside tool categories.
Enable Group tools by type first, then enable Favorites in grouped tools.
Add tools to favorites from the tool list; use Show favorite as last to move this tab to the end.
The favorites tab can be placed after the other main-screen tabs.
Enable Show favorite as last to move the favorites tab to the end, or disable it to place it first.
In grouped mode, enable Favorites in grouped tools first; otherwise there is no favorites tab to move.
Resize presets store percentage sizes that can be reused instead of entering dimensions for every image.
Open Presets to edit the available values. A value of 50 means half the original width and height; 125 enlarges them to 125%.
Select a preset in a compatible resize tool and check the resulting dimensions before saving.
Default quality initializes compression controls and depends on the selected output format.
Choose Default Image Format first, then adjust the quality controls shown for that format.
Use the tool’s own quality selector for a one-off export; a quality number is not a guaranteed file-size limit.
Text-layer defaults reduce repeated setup when adding text in Markup Layers.
Open Markup Layers in Default values and set text appearance, alignment, color and size.
Expand the optional transformation, shadow and outline controls if needed, then close the sheet and add a new text layer to check the defaults.
Orientation lock prevents screen rotation from interrupting drawing.
Enable Lock draw orientation before working with drawing controls.
Disable it when you need the drawing screen to follow device rotation again.
The default draw color is the starting color for drawing controls.
Open Default Draw Color and select a color in the picker.
Check it on a new drawing; changing the current tool’s color remains available for individual strokes.
The default path mode selects the drawing behavior initially offered by drawing tools.
Select a mode from Default Draw Path Mode.
Open a drawing tool and confirm the active mode; switch modes there when a different mark or shape is needed.
The drawing magnifier helps place marks precisely when a finger obscures the canvas.
Enable Magnifier, then touch or draw on a supported drawing canvas.
Disable it if the enlarged view gets in the way; zooming the canvas remains a separate action.
A thin canvas border makes the image boundary easier to see while drawing or erasing.
Enable Drawing border and inspect the edge of the drawing or erasing canvas.
Turn it off for an unobstructed canvas view; it is an editor guide, not a frame added to the saved image.
This sets the initial keep-metadata choice in tools that show the EXIF widget.
Turn off Always clear EXIF before changing Force initial value.
Enable it to start with metadata preservation selected; check the EXIF choice again before exporting sensitive photos.
Capture date/time can be preserved separately from the ordinary keep-EXIF choice.
Disable Always clear EXIF, then enable Keep Date Time when capture dates must survive export.
To remove dates, disable both this option and EXIF preservation in the tool, or enable Always clear EXIF. The latter takes precedence and disables this control.
Export metadata can record the app version and configured image parameters.
Disable Always clear EXIF before enabling Add ImageToolbox metadata.
Enable it for traceable exports, or leave it off when the saved file should not identify the app and processing parameters.
This option removes successfully processed source files after their results are saved.
Open Settings → Folder and turn Delete original files after saving on or off. It is unavailable while Overwrite Files is active.
For ordinary copies leave it off. If enabled, check the saved result and keep a separate backup of originals you need to retain.
A prefix helps distinguish generated copies from originals in a folder.
Open Prefix, enter the text, and confirm; leading and trailing spaces are trimmed.
Disable Randomize filename, Checksum as Filename or Overwrite Files if the field is unavailable. Check Filename Format when a custom pattern omits the prefix.
A suffix labels edited copies near the end of their filename.
Open Suffix, enter a label such as edited, and confirm.
Use ordinary filename behavior to enable this field; for a custom Filename Format, include the suffix token in the pattern.
Despite the name, this switch inserts image width and height, not the file size in bytes.
Enable Add file size with ordinary filename behavior to include output dimensions.
Check the name preview or a test export. Random and checksum filenames do not use these ordinary name components.
The original name can be retained in generated filenames to keep copies traceable.
Enable Add original filename while ordinary filename behavior is selected.
Combine it with a suffix, timestamp or sequence for batches; files created without a source do not have an original name to insert.
Batch sequence numbers can replace the standard timestamp component.
Enable Replace sequence number when ordered output names are more useful than timestamps.
Test a batch and check the resulting order; use ordinary filename behavior and a compatible Filename Format.
Timestamps help separate repeated exports of the same source.
Enable Add Timestamp in Filename settings.
Enable Formatted Timestamp for a readable date/time, or leave it off for the basic millisecond representation; sequence replacement can change batch naming.
Formatted timestamps replace the raw millisecond value with readable date/time text.
Enable Add Timestamp first; Formatted Timestamp is disabled otherwise.
Turn formatting on and inspect the filename preview. Special random, checksum and overwrite modes do not use these ordinary naming controls.
Preset information can be included in output names when a resize preset was used.
Enable Add Preset To Filename with ordinary filename behavior.
Choose a preset in a supported resize tool; without a preset there is no preset information to append.
Scale-mode names can identify which resizing method produced an output.
Enable Add Image Scale Mode To Filename with ordinary filename behavior.
Export from a tool that provides a scale mode. The inserted mode name uses English and hyphens in place of spaces.
The filename can be derived from the checksum of the encoded output bytes.
Turn off random or overwrite naming, enable Checksum as Filename, and choose a hashing algorithm in the expanded selector.
This replaces the ordinary prefix/suffix/pattern name. Disable it to restore those controls; it is naming, not encryption.
Random naming produces an unrelated 32-character name while retaining the output extension.
Disable checksum or overwrite naming, then enable Randomize filename.
Turn it off when names must remain associated with originals; ordinary filename fields are disabled while random naming is active.
Manual cache clearing removes temporary app data and updates the displayed cache size.
Open Settings → Storage → Cache and tap the row to run cleanup.
Wait for the size to update. This control is separate from Reset settings and from deleting your exported files.
Automatic cleanup uses both a cache size threshold and a checking interval.
Enable Auto cache clearing to activate Cache limit and Cleanup interval.
Choose both values; turning automatic cleanup off leaves manual Cache clearing available.
The interval controls when automatic cleanup checks are due, not a timer for deleting exported images.
Enable Auto cache clearing, open Cleanup interval and choose every app launch, day, week or month.
Set Cache limit separately; an interval becoming due does not by itself mean the size threshold has been exceeded.
Restore reads an ImageToolbox settings backup and applies its saved preferences.
Open Restore and choose a backup previously created by the app. Keep a current backup first if you may need to undo the replacement.
After successful restoration the screen is recreated. Re-select Output folder: the stored folder URI is cleared during restore.
Reset returns app preferences to their defaults after confirmation.
Create a settings Backup if you may want to recover the current configuration.
Open Reset and confirm the dialog only when ready; use Restore with that backup to recover saved preferences later.
Crash collection is controlled independently from usage analytics in builds that include Firebase.
Open Firebase → Crashlytics and choose whether automatic crash reports are allowed.
This group is absent in FOSS builds. For a specific report, Send Logs remains an explicit sharing action.
The analytics switch controls anonymous usage collection in builds that include Firebase.
Open Firebase → Analytics to enable or disable collection.
This setting is separate from Crashlytics and the local Usage Statistics screen; the Firebase group is not shown in FOSS builds.
Automatic update checks control whether an available update is announced at startup.
Enable Check for updates in the Updates group to allow startup checks.
Use the separate Check for updates button for an immediate check; finding an update does not silently install it.
Beta releases can be included in the app’s update search.
Enable Allow betas to include beta releases, or disable it to prefer stable releases.
Changing the switch triggers another update check. This row is hidden for installations recognized as coming from Google Play.
The manual update button starts a check immediately instead of waiting for app startup.
Open Updates and press the Check for updates button.
Review the result and any release information; enable Allow betas only if pre-release builds should be included.
The version row shows which ImageToolbox build is installed.
Open About app and read the version row when reporting a bug or comparing builds.
Tap the row for an update check; use App Logs or Send Logs for diagnostic details rather than guessing the version.
Usage Statistics shows local app opens, tool launches and frequently used tools.
Open About app → Usage Statistics to inspect the recorded activity.
Use the screen’s own filters and controls; this navigation entry is separate from the Firebase Analytics collection switch.
The log viewer is useful for inspecting errors without sending a report immediately.
Open About app → App Logs after reproducing the problem.
Review the relevant entries. Use Send Logs when you want to share a file with a report; merely opening logs sends nothing.
The licenses screen lists the open-source libraries used by the app.
Open About app → Open Source Licenses.
Select a library to inspect its available information and license before reusing its code.
Translation contributions are made through the project’s Weblate page.
Open Help translate to launch the translation site.
Choose the language and string there; changing a translation on the site does not immediately replace the installed app resources.
Bug reports and feature requests go to the project’s issue tracker.
Open Issue tracker and check whether a matching issue already exists.
Include app version, Android version and reproducible steps; attach logs when relevant. Opening the page does not submit a report.
This entry opens the partner’s software channel when the entry is available.
Open Free Software (Partner) from About app.
It is shown only for Russian locale in non-FOSS builds; it is an external link, not an ImageToolbox editing tool.
The Telegram group is the community discussion destination.
Open Telegram chat to launch the group link.
Read or compose a message in Telegram; the app does not post a message automatically. Use Issue tracker for a structured bug report.
The channel is for project announcements and release news.
Open CI channel from About app to launch its Telegram link.
Use the Telegram chat for discussion or the Updates group to check the installed build against available releases.
The source-code entry opens the project repository.
Open Source code in About app to browse the repository in a browser.
Use the repository’s code and release information as needed; this action does not change the installed app.
Help & Tips contains task instructions and direct links to relevant tools and settings.
Open Help & Tips, choose a category or search for a task or setting name.
Read the steps and use the page’s open action to continue in the app; opening a tool does not perform the operation automatically.
The debug menu exposes development test actions, including deliberate failure cases.
Open Debug Menu only in a debug build; the entry is absent from production settings.
Read each test action before running it. It is not required for normal editing or troubleshooting with logs.
Clipboard-only output skips storage saving and attempts to put the result on the clipboard.
Enable Auto pin first, then enable Only Clip.
Use it when a clipboard result is sufficient; disable it before saving if you need a persistent image file in the output folder.
Haptic strength adjusts the app’s vibration feedback where it is supported.
Move Vibration Strength in the 0–2 range; zero disables the app feedback.
Try a control that produces haptics and adjust the strength for your device. System or device restrictions may still prevent vibration.
Brightness enforcement is selected per tool instead of being a global brightness slider.
Open Brightness Enforcement and select the tools that should use enforced brightness.
Unselect a tool to let it return to ordinary brightness behavior; an empty selection disables enforcement for all tools.
System bars can be shown or hidden to trade navigation chrome for working space.
Choose one of the displayed visibility modes for status/navigation bars.
If you hide bars, configure Show System Bars By Swipe separately and check that your normal navigation gestures remain usable.
This switch chooses transient system bars revealed by an edge swipe instead of Android’s default bar behavior.
Select a mode that hides system bars, then enable Show System Bars By Swipe.
Swipe from the corresponding edge to reveal the bars temporarily. Turn the switch off to use Android’s default behavior instead.
Choose the emoji decoration used in the app interface, or remove it from the selector.
Disable Random Emojis first if manual selection is unavailable, then open Emoji and choose an item.
Choose the no-emoji item to hide the decoration; count and animation controls become available when an emoji is selected.
The emoji count controls how many decorative emoji appear together in the interface.
Select an emoji first so the count control becomes available.
Choose a count from 1 to 5; this changes interface decoration rather than adding emoji to exported images.
Animated emoji uses an animated variant of the selected decoration when one is available.
Select an emoji, then enable Animated Emojis.
Disable the switch for a static decoration; some emoji may not have an animated variant.
Random emoji replaces manual decoration selection with a randomly chosen emoji.
Select an emoji to enable the decoration, then turn on Random Emojis.
Turn the switch off before choosing a specific emoji manually; the manual selector is disabled while random selection is active.
Confetti controls the app’s celebratory particle animation.
Enable Confetti to use the animation and unlock its type and color controls.
Disable it to remove this decoration; the switch does not change the processed image.
The confetti harmonizer selects the color used to tint the particle palette.
Enable Confetti, then choose a listed harmonization color or use the custom-color picker.
Adjust Harmonization Level separately to control how strongly that color affects the particles.
Harmonization level changes the strength of the selected confetti color adjustment.
Enable Confetti and choose its harmonization color first.
Move the level from 0 to 1: lower values retain more of the original particle palette, higher values apply more harmonization.
Confetti type chooses which particle shapes the celebration uses.
Enable Confetti so the type selector is available.
Open Confetti Type and select one of the displayed particle sets; color and harmonization remain separate settings.
When ImageToolbox was opened by another app, this setting allows returning to that app after a successful save.
Enable Return After Save when completing edits started from another app.
Disable it if you want to stay in ImageToolbox and continue working after saving; ordinary launches have no external app to return to.
Landscape settings visibility controls the settings panel used in the horizontal layout.
Disable Fullscreen Settings if this option is unavailable.
Enable or disable Show Settings In Landscape, then rotate the device to check the resulting layout.
The side button opens quick settings from a tool without leaving the current screen.
Enable Side Button and choose Start or End to place it at the corresponding side of the interface.
Open a tool and tap the edge control. Disable the setting to hide quick settings; Assistant has its own enable switch.
Assistant answers questions about ImageToolbox using a downloaded local model. Ordinary models use documentation and file metadata; Vision models also analyze an attached photo.
Open Assistant from the main screen or a tool. Choose Lite, Advanced or Max for text, or Vision Lite, Vision Advanced or Vision Max for image understanding, then download the model.
Ask how to complete a task and open the suggested links yourself. To ask about visible contents, choose a Vision model and attach one photo; ordinary models receive file metadata instead of pixels.
After the model download, conversations can run offline. Use the model selector to switch models, manage downloads or remove installed files.
Snowfall adds an interface decoration according to the selected mode.
Open Snowfall and choose one of the displayed modes, including the disabled mode when no snow is wanted.
Return to the app interface to inspect the effect; snowfall does not become part of exported images.
Link previews can display additional information for detected web links.
Enable Link Previews when you want preview cards for supported links.
Disable it to avoid fetching preview content; the detected link text remains available for normal actions.
Sheet gestures allow dragging bottom sheets to change or dismiss their visible state.
Enable Sheet Gestures, then drag the handle of a bottom sheet to use its supported gestures.
Disable the switch if accidental drags interrupt selection; the sheet’s explicit buttons remain available.
Nested scrolling lets scrolling content participate in moving its containing bottom sheet.
Enable Sheet Gestures, then enable Nested Scrolling to let a scroll gesture transfer to the sheet at the content boundary.
Disable Nested Scrolling if you want to scroll the contents without that transfer; use the sheet handle or buttons for other actions.
Embedded preview loads the camera’s ready-made preview instead of developing the RAW sensor data.
Enable Embedded Preview when a camera-rendered preview is sufficient; its dimensions and appearance may differ from full RAW development.
Disable it to use white balance, color space, exposure, demosaicing and other RAW development settings, which are unavailable in preview mode.
RAW output color space selects the color space used when developing sensor data.
Disable Embedded Preview, then select sRGB, Adobe RGB, Wide Gamut RGB, ProPhoto RGB, CIE XYZ or ACES.
Use sRGB for a conventional output or a wider space when your later workflow supports it; this setting does not choose the exported file format.
Highlight recovery selects how RAW development handles bright regions near clipping.
Disable Embedded Preview and compare Clip, Unclip, Blend and Reconstruct on a RAW with bright detail.
For Reconstruct, adjust its level from 3 to 9. Inspect both highlight detail and color; the setting cannot guarantee recovery of missing sensor information.
Exposure compensation adjusts RAW development brightness in exposure-value steps.
Disable Embedded Preview, then set Exposure Compensation between −2 and +3 EV; zero leaves this adjustment neutral.
Compare shadows and highlights after changing it. If bright detail needs separate treatment, use Highlight Recovery or Highlight Preservation.
Highlight preservation controls the protection of bright tones during RAW exposure adjustment.
Disable Embedded Preview, then adjust Highlight Preservation from 0 to 1.
Compare it together with Exposure Compensation on the same RAW; this control is separate from the Highlight Recovery mode.
