Automatic brightness lets RAW development choose brightness; turning it off exposes a manual multiplier.
Disable Embedded Preview and enable Automatic Brightness for automatic adjustment.
Turn it off to set Brightness from 0.1 to 4; compare the result before applying further exposure corrections.
Demosaicing chooses the algorithm that reconstructs colors from RAW sensor samples.
Disable Embedded Preview, then select Linear, VNG, PPG, AHD, DCB, DHT or AAHD in Demosaic Quality.
Compare fine edges, color artifacts and processing time on your camera’s files; choose the result that suits your images rather than treating the list as file-quality percentages.
Half-size RAW development reduces output dimensions to lower the decoding workload.
Disable Embedded Preview, then enable Half Size when full resolution is unnecessary.
Disable it before an export that needs full dimensions. Check the developed image dimensions rather than assuming the camera preview and RAW output are identical.
RAW orientation applies the rotation or mirror information recorded by the camera during development.
Disable Embedded Preview and enable Apply Orientation for the camera’s recorded orientation.
Disable it when you intentionally want the decoded orientation without that adjustment; use an editing tool if a further rotation is needed.
Make the whole image translucent with the Opacity filter
To change a photo’s transparency, open Filter and add Opacity in Full Filter mode. Lower opacity makes the whole image more transparent.
Open this page’s tool link to start with Opacity selected. Choose a photo, then adjust the filter. When opening Filter manually, use Full Filter → Add filter → Opacity.
Adjust Opacity from 0 to 1: 1 keeps the original opacity, 0.5 makes it half opaque, and 0 makes it invisible.
Save as PNG to keep transparency. If Background Color For Alpha Formats is enabled, choose a fully transparent background or disable that setting before export; JPEG cannot store transparency.
Disable shadows for cards, bars, buttons, switches and sliders
Interface shadows have six independent switches in Settings → Shadows. Turn off all six to disable the configured shadows throughout the interface; there is no single master shadow switch.
Open Settings → Shadows. The link on this page opens the Containers switch in that section.
Turn off Containers, App bars, Buttons, FABs, Switches and Sliders. To remove only one kind of shadow, turn off its corresponding switch.
If Shadows is hidden or a switch is unavailable, open Secondary Customization and set Border thickness to 0 to access these controls. Changes affect the app interface, not shadows inside your photos.
Compresses the tonal range with the ACES filmic curve. Exposure controls the brightness entering the curve; compare highlights and shadow detail. This cannot recover clipped source data.
Compresses the tonal range with the ACES Hill curve. Exposure controls the brightness entering the curve; compare highlights and shadow detail. This cannot recover clipped source data.

Approximates the color appearance of reduced color discrimination across the spectrum using a fixed color matrix. Useful when checking whether a design relies only on color; it is not an individual vision assessment.
Approximates the color appearance of absence of color discrimination using a fixed color matrix. Useful when checking whether a design relies only on color; it is not an individual vision assessment.
Smooths nearby pixels with similar colors while keeping stronger boundaries. Radius sets the neighborhood; threshold controls how different the colors may be before they stop blending.
Maps tonal range with the Aldridge curve. Exposure sets the input brightness and cutoff adjusts the lower end of the mapping. Check dark detail after changing the cutoff.
Applies a built-in LUT with deep cool shadows and slightly green middle tones. Strength blends between the original colors at zero and the full color grade at one.
Separates red and cyan copies of the image horizontally for an anaglyph-style colour fringe. Strength controls their offset; this is a colour effect, not depth reconstruction from a single photo.
Smooths small variations while treating strong boundaries differently from flat areas. More iterations increase smoothing; conduction and diffusion control how far neighboring tones mix.
Bends the image into an arc. Radius and size define the curved strip, spread angle determines how far it wraps, and angle and centre position place it in the frame.

Rebuilds the picture from characters. Font size determines detail, the character gradient maps brightness, and the background and grayscale options control the appearance; the result remains an image.

Uses Atkinson error diffusion to represent intermediate tones with a pattern of pixels. Threshold changes the tonal split; grayscale removes color before dithering. Compare the grain pattern at full size.

Finds horizontal image boundaries and crops the top and bottom automatically, retaining the full width. Tolerance changes edge-detection sensitivity; use manual cropping when the detected region does not match the subject.
Detects perspective distortion and attempts to straighten the image automatically. Check the result on scenes without clear straight lines; the filter has no manual corner controls.
Attempts to suppress red pupils automatically. The threshold controls which red areas qualify; inspect the preview because small eyes may be missed and other red details may change.

Automatically adjusts the color balance. Strength blends the correction, while clipping controls how extreme tones influence the estimate; check naturally colored lighting before applying a strong correction.
Maps image brightness to red to yellow. This false-color palette replaces the original colors; useful for making tonal differences visible or creating a graphic effect.
Mixes colors toward muted warm autumn tones.
Shows the difference between each pixel and the average of its four neighbors. Useful for inspecting fine detail and noise; bright regions alone do not prove that a photo was edited.
Uses a repeating 8 × 8 Bayer threshold matrix to form ordered pixel patterns. Threshold controls the tonal split and grayscale switches to monochrome output.
Uses a repeating 4 × 4 Bayer threshold matrix to form ordered pixel patterns. Threshold controls the tonal split and grayscale switches to monochrome output.
Uses a repeating 3 × 3 Bayer threshold matrix to form ordered pixel patterns. Threshold controls the tonal split and grayscale switches to monochrome output.
Uses a repeating 2 × 2 Bayer threshold matrix to form ordered pixel patterns. Threshold controls the tonal split and grayscale switches to monochrome output.

Smooths noise while keeping color boundaries. Radius sets the neighborhood, sigma controls the allowed color difference, and spatial sigma controls the influence of distant pixels. Large values can erase fine texture.
Converts colors to shades of gray according to their brightness. Use it for a monochrome photo; it keeps intermediate gray tones rather than producing a two-color stencil.
Extracts dark details smaller than the selected neighborhood by subtracting the image from its morphological closing. Kernel size and circular or square shape determine which structures stand out.
Applies a built-in LUT with strong brightening and high tonal contrast. Strength blends between the original colors at zero and the full color grade at one.
Breaks the image into displaced blocks for a digital corruption effect. Block size controls the size of the fragments, while strength controls the distortion.
Spreads a glow from bright areas. Threshold selects the highlights, radius sets the spread, strength sets its intensity, and soft knee smooths the transition around the threshold.

Expands bright details with a polygon-shaped kernel to create bokeh-like spots. Size controls the spot size and amount controls the number of polygon sides; this does not detect a subject or a background.

Adds generated bokeh lights over the image. Adjust their count, radius, aperture blades and color; seed changes their arrangement. These lights are added decoratively rather than detected in the photo.
Maps image brightness to black through cool gray to white. This false-color palette replaces the original colors; useful for making tonal differences visible or creating a graphic effect.
Adds a solid border outside the image, increasing its dimensions. Horizontal and vertical thickness control the two pairs of sides; the color picker sets the border color.
Blurs by averaging pixels in a square neighborhood. Increase the value for a wider blur; edges and fine detail are softened along with noise.
Adds or subtracts brightness across the image. Zero leaves brightness unchanged; positive values lighten and negative values darken. Strong adjustments can clip shadows or highlights.

Displaces the image inside irregular cells. Frequency controls cell density, variability changes their shape, distortion changes the deformation within each cell, and seed selects a different arrangement.
Splits the image into irregular glass-like shards that shift and rotate the content. Frequency changes shard density, intensity controls their displacement, and seed changes the fracture pattern.
Remixes color channels into a subdued brown-green palette.
Bulges or pinches a circular area in the centre of the image. Radius sets the affected area and the sign of scale changes the direction of the deformation.

Uses Burkes error diffusion to represent intermediate tones with a pattern of pixels. Threshold changes the tonal split; grayscale removes color before dithering. Compare the grain pattern at full size.
Applies a built-in LUT with warm brown-gold middle tones and subdued brightness. Strength blends between the original colors at zero and the full color grade at one.
Produces an edge map using two detection thresholds. Raise the thresholds to reject weak edges and noise; lower them to retain more faint boundaries.
Strengthens warm reddish tones while reducing the green contribution.
Applies a built-in LUT with cool shadows and brighter middle tones. Strength blends between the original colors at zero and the full color grade at one.
Reduces the image to a small, bright palette inspired by CGA computer graphics. Use it for a retro game look; smooth color transitions become abrupt.
Redistributes red, green and blue contributions between output channels. Use the channel mixing controls for deliberate color shifts rather than uniform brightness adjustment.
Gives tonal transitions a reflective chrome-like appearance. Amount and exposure control the metallic contrast; the effect changes the picture rather than reconstructing real reflections.
Blends neighboring pixels using a filled circular kernel. Increasing the size spreads the effect farther and changes how small bright details are smeared.
Replaces image detail with circular cells. Increase cell size for a coarser dotted mosaic; small text and fine contours become harder to distinguish.
Reflects image details across a circular boundary. Radius places the boundary, mode selects inward or outward reflection, and intensity blends the coordinate distortion with the original geometry.
Maps image brightness to dark blue through gray-green to yellow. This false-color palette replaces the original colors; useful for making tonal differences visible or creating a graphic effect.
Increases local contrast with contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization in RGB. Grid sizes divide the image into regions and threshold limits contrast amplification.

Increases local contrast with contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization in HSL. Grid sizes divide the image into regions and threshold limits contrast amplification. Bins set histogram resolution.

Increases local contrast with contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization in HSV. Grid sizes divide the image into regions and threshold limits contrast amplification. Bins set histogram resolution.

Increases local contrast with contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization in Jzazbz. Grid sizes divide the image into regions and threshold limits contrast amplification. Bins set histogram resolution.

Increases local contrast with contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization in Lab. Grid sizes divide the image into regions and threshold limits contrast amplification. Bins set histogram resolution.

Increases local contrast with contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization in Luv. Grid sizes divide the image into regions and threshold limits contrast amplification. Bins set histogram resolution.

Increases local contrast with contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization in Oklab. Grid sizes divide the image into regions and threshold limits contrast amplification. Bins set histogram resolution.

Increases local contrast with contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization in Oklch. Grid sizes divide the image into regions and threshold limits contrast amplification. Bins set histogram resolution.
Dilates then erodes the image to close small dark gaps in bright regions. Neighborhood size and shape determine how large a gap is affected.
Uses a 2 × 2 clustered-dot pattern to represent tones, similar to a small printing screen. Adjust threshold for the tonal split and enable grayscale for a monochrome result.
Uses a 4 × 4 clustered-dot pattern to represent tones, similar to a small printing screen. Adjust threshold for the tonal split and enable grayscale for a monochrome result.
Uses a 8 × 8 clustered-dot pattern to represent tones, similar to a small printing screen. Adjust threshold for the tonal split and enable grayscale for a monochrome result.
Separates color channels more strongly for a saturated film-like palette.
Applies a built-in LUT with warm brown middle tones and subdued whites. Strength blends between the original colors at zero and the full color grade at one.
Applies a strong nonlinear colour transformation for unnatural colour shifts. Strength changes the colour cutoff used by the effect; use it for stylisation rather than colour correction.
Changes the color balance separately in highlights, midtones and shadows. Adjust the tonal region containing the unwanted cast instead of tinting the whole image equally.
Strongly mixes green and blue into red for a bright, warm color shift.
Paints a uniform color over the image. The chosen color’s alpha determines how much of the original remains visible, making this useful for tinting or translucent overlays.
Simulates color printing with separate cyan, magenta and yellow dot screens. Radius sets dot size; the three angles rotate the screens and change their overlap.
Applies a color-channel mask using the chosen color. This changes the retained channel values across the image; it does not select a matching object or background.
Mixes RGB channels through a three-by-three matrix. Diagonal coefficients scale their own channels; other coefficients transfer color between channels for custom color corrections.
Transforms color and alpha with a four-by-four matrix. Unlike the RGB matrix, coefficients can also affect transparency; inspect the result on a transparent background.
Replaces colors with a stepped palette made from shades of the chosen color. Strength changes the spacing of those shades, producing more or less pronounced posterization.
Mixes neighboring RGB channels to change color relationships. It changes colors without twisting the picture.

Stretches sampled rows into vertical columns of stepped colour bands. Count sets the number of columns, variability changes the band spacing between columns, and intensity controls how strongly the original detail is flattened.

Offsets and rotates concentric circular bands to create broken rings. Frequency controls the number of bands, distortion changes their rotation, and dampening reduces the effect farther from the centre.
Offsets and rotates concentric square bands. Frequency controls band density, distortion adds rotation, and dampening reduces the displacement away from the centre.
Draws contour lines along tonal levels. Levels control their number, scale and offset shift the pattern, and the selected color sets the line color.
Changes the separation between light and dark tones. One keeps the original contrast; smaller values flatten the image and larger values increase contrast. Watch for lost shadow and highlight detail.
Applies a custom three-by-three kernel to neighboring pixels. Use coefficient patterns for sharpening, blur or edge detection; large sums can clip brightness and negative weights can create halos.
Reduces warm channels and boosts blue for a cooler overall tone.
Maps image brightness to cyan to magenta. This false-color palette replaces the original colors; useful for making tonal differences visible or creating a graphic effect.
Highlights regions with similarities that may indicate copied image content. Detection parameters change sensitivity; repeated natural patterns can also match, so the result is not proof of editing.

Selects a four-corner region and straightens it into a rectangle, which is useful for a tilted document or sign. Set all four corners around the desired region and choose whether coordinates are relative to the image or absolute pixels.
Removes outer areas matching the selected ignored colour. Tolerance allows nearby colours to be treated as the same background; increasing it too far can also remove similarly coloured edge details.
Blends neighboring pixels using a cross-shaped kernel. Increasing the size spreads the effect farther and changes how small bright details are smeared.
Replaces fine detail with a cross-shaped cell pattern. Cell size determines the scale of the mosaic; increasing it makes the crosses more prominent and reduces recognizable detail.
Turns tonal differences into crossed black lines on a light background. Spacing sets the distance between lines and line width controls their thickness.
Imitates a curved CRT screen with darkened edges and colour-channel separation. Curvature bends the image, vignette darkens the perimeter, and chroma adjusts the coloured fringes.
Divides the image into irregular colored crystal-like regions. Cluster density controls detail, and the stroke color makes the boundaries between regions visible.

Applies color grading from a .cube LUT file. Select a file or an installed LUT, then adjust strength from the original colors at zero to the full transformation at one. A LUT changes colors, not image geometry.
Cross-mixes RGB channels with stronger red-blue interaction for stylized neon-like colors.
Maps image brightness to black through green to pale tones. This false-color palette replaces the original colors; useful for making tonal differences visible or creating a graphic effect.
Adds red-blue cross-mixing for a pronounced purple color cast.
Reduces the washed-out appearance of haze. Radius sets the neighborhood used for the estimate and the strength parameter controls correction; excessive values can darken the picture unnaturally.
Estimates the tilt of the image and rotates it to straighten detected lines. The maximum angle limits the correction; allowing cropping removes the empty corners introduced by rotation.
Removes small isolated specks by comparing neighboring pixels. Useful for scattered noise; inspect thin lines and tiny details because they may also be smoothed.

Approximates the color appearance of reduced green-color discrimination using a fixed color matrix. Useful when checking whether a design relies only on color; it is not an individual vision assessment.

Approximates the color appearance of absence of green-color discrimination using a fixed color matrix. Useful when checking whether a design relies only on color; it is not an individual vision assessment.
Rebuilds detail as diamond-shaped cells. Cell size controls mosaic coarseness; use a small size when recognizable contours matter.
Randomly displaces nearby pixels for a frosted-glass texture. Scale controls how far pixels can move; it scatters detail rather than simply softening it.
Remaps green strongly into red and blue, creating unusual color separation. It does not add text or symbols.
Expands brighter regions using a circular or square neighborhood. Larger kernels thicken bright lines and close gaps, and can alter transparency when the image has an alpha channel.

Warps the image using a selected displacement map, with a separate vertical map available if needed. Horizontal and vertical strength control movement along each axis; interpolation affects smoothness and boundary mode determines how pixels outside the image are sampled.
Breaks the image into randomly transparent fragments. Density controls how much remains and softness changes the transition; save to a transparency-capable format to retain the holes.
Warps the entire image into a quadrilateral defined by four corner positions. Use it to simulate perspective; clipping controls whether the transformed result is cut to the image bounds.
Uses content-aware seam processing to distort the image rather than applying a uniform geometric warp. Strength controls the distortion amount; larger values can noticeably reshape objects.
Subtracts two Gaussian-blurred versions to emphasize structures between their scales. The two radii select the detail band; similar radii produce a weaker difference.
Compresses bright tones with the Drago tone-mapping curve. Exposure changes input brightness and threshold sets the white point used by the mapping.
Applies a built-in LUT with compressed tonal contrast and modified blue colors. Strength blends between the original colors at zero and the full color grade at one.
Adds a shadow from the image’s alpha silhouette and expands the canvas so it is not clipped. Color, blur radius and horizontal/vertical offsets control the shadow.
Applies a built-in LUT with a strong amber-yellow cast. Strength blends between the original colors at zero and the full color grade at one.
Brightens and softens color separation by mixing a little of each RGB channel into the others. It does not draw a gradient.
Turns brightness changes into a raised or engraved relief. Intensity controls the strength; flat areas lose much of their original color detail.
Applies the enhanced circular-cell mosaic. Increase cell size to remove fine detail and emphasize the dot pattern; compare with ordinary circle pixelation to choose the preferred rendering.
Applies the enhanced diamond-cell mosaic. Cell size controls the scale of the pattern and the amount of retained detail.

Combines shifted colour channels with displaced rectangular fragments. Corruption size and amount control the fragment size and count, while shift controls set the displacement for a stronger digital-glitch appearance.
Groups nearby tones into an oil-paint-like texture. The oil range controls the neighborhood size; larger values merge small details into broader painted areas.
Applies the enhanced square-cell mosaic. Increase cell size for larger blocks and fewer fine details without changing the image’s intended composition.
Stretches detail outward from a chosen center, with an additional angle control. Center X/Y place the effect; radius, sigma and strength control its spread and intensity.
Redistributes tonal levels using the image histogram to increase contrast in a dull image. The adjustment is automatic and can also emphasize noise or change the color balance.
Equalizes the image histogram automatically to use more of the available tonal range. Useful for low-contrast images; check colors and noise after the adjustment.
Equalizes local contrast in RGB across a grid of image regions. Grid X/Y set the subdivision. Unlike CLAHE, this filter has no contrast limit and can emphasize noise.
Equalizes local contrast in HSL across a grid of image regions. Grid X/Y set the subdivision. Unlike CLAHE, this filter has no contrast limit and can emphasize noise.
Equalizes local contrast in HSV across a grid of image regions. Grid X/Y set the subdivision. Unlike CLAHE, this filter has no contrast limit and can emphasize noise.
Equalizes local contrast in Lab across a grid of image regions. Grid X/Y set the subdivision. Unlike CLAHE, this filter has no contrast limit and can emphasize noise.
Equalizes local contrast in Luv across a grid of image regions. Grid X/Y set the subdivision. Unlike CLAHE, this filter has no contrast limit and can emphasize noise.
Equalizes brightness in HSV color space. The number of bins controls histogram resolution; color appearance can still change when bright or saturated regions are pushed too far.
Equalizes tones separately in a rectangular grid, creating a tiled contrast effect. Horizontal and vertical grid counts control how many regions receive independent correction.
Shrinks brighter regions using a circular or square neighborhood. Larger kernels thin bright lines and expand dark regions; alpha information can also be affected.
Shows differences introduced by JPEG recompression at the selected quality. Bright differences can come from texture or previous compression as well as editing, so they are not proof of manipulation.

Enlarges the canvas on each side and fills the new area using textures sampled from the original image. Set the added pixels separately for left, top, right and bottom; the generated border works best with textures and does not reconstruct unseen objects.

Adjusts exposure by multiplying brightness, similar to changing exposure stops. Zero is neutral; positive values brighten and negative values darken. It cannot recover detail already clipped in the source.
Applies a built-in LUT with warm beige-brown tones. Strength blends between the original colors at zero and the full color grade at one.
Maps dark and light areas to two chosen colors. Use it for a duotone illustration or to separate tonal regions; the colors are artificial and do not represent measured temperature.

Uses False Floyd–Steinberg error diffusion to represent intermediate tones with a pattern of pixels. Threshold changes the tonal split; grayscale removes color before dithering. Compare the grain pattern at full size.
Cross-mixes colors toward warm reds and cooler blues for a stylized palette. It does not add landscape details.

Applies a fast bilateral smoothing pass that considers both pixel distance and color difference. Size sets the neighborhood; sigma and spatial sigma adjust the smoothing. Compare fine textures before saving.
Creates a broad blur with an adjustable processing scale. Radius controls blur strength; reducing scale trades fine detail for faster processing.
Approximates Gaussian blur with a degree-2 fast filter. Radius sets the smoothing width. The degree describes the approximation, not the dimensions of the image.
Approximates Gaussian blur with a degree-3 fast filter. Radius sets the smoothing width. The degree describes the approximation, not the dimensions of the image.
Approximates Gaussian blur with a degree-4 fast filter. Radius sets the smoothing width. The degree describes the approximation, not the dimensions of the image.
Layers repeated transformed copies of the image to produce a visual echo. Distance and angle set the direction of the copies, while rotation and zoom create a twisting or receding trail.
Applies a built-in LUT with bright warm middle tones and deep shadows. Strength blends between the original colors at zero and the full color grade at one.
Adds generated firework bursts. Explosion and particle counts set their density, time selects the stage of the burst, and seed changes the arrangement. The output remains a still image.
Adds a lens flare at a chosen position. Radius sets its size; base, ring and ray amounts control the components, with separate ring width and color.

Uses Floyd–Steinberg error diffusion to represent intermediate tones with a pattern of pixels. Threshold changes the tonal split; grayscale removes color before dithering. Compare the grain pattern at full size.
Applies a built-in LUT with lifted blue shadows and dark middle tones. Strength blends between the original colors at zero and the full color grade at one.
Distorts the image as if seen through irregular textured glass. Strength controls the glass-pattern size and amplitude controls the displacement of the details.
Mixes red and blue with a slight green contribution for a cool stylized palette. It changes colors without adding shapes.

Repeatedly moves image details along changes in brightness, producing flowing, melted contours. Iterations increase the number of passes and intensity controls the distance and direction of each pass.
Changes the distribution of middle tones with gamma correction. One is neutral; adjust while watching the midtones rather than treating it as an exposure control.
Smooths the whole image with a Gaussian blur. Radius sets the neighborhood and sigma controls the spread; edge mode determines how pixels outside the image are treated.
Approximates Gaussian smoothing with repeated box blurs. Sigma controls the width of the blur; use it for broad softening without preserving sharp edges.
Refracts the image through a repeating grid of hexagonal glass tiles. Frequency changes tile density, intensity controls the base refraction, and distortion changes the deformation inside each tile.
Refracts the image through a grid of rectangular glass tiles. Frequency controls how many tiles appear, while intensity and distortion adjust the displacement within each tile.
Makes a central circular area look like a glass sphere refracting the image underneath. Radius controls the sphere size and refractive index changes how strongly the image bends inside it.

Refracts image details through a repeating triangular tile pattern. Frequency changes the number of triangles, intensity sets the refraction strength, and distortion changes the deformation within them.

Creates JPEG-style corruption by modifying encoded image data. Amount and iterations control the extent of the disruption, while seed selects a different repeatable pattern of damaged bands and colours.

Combines repeated image shifts with separated colour channels. Repeat count controls the number of disruptions, maximum offset limits their displacement, and channel shift controls the coloured fringes.
Blends a softened glow into the original image. Amount controls how strongly the glow brightens and softens the result.

Runs the G’MIC commands you enter, optionally with additional input images. The result depends on the command and input order; invalid commands report an error rather than selecting a built-in preset.
Sharpens detail across several scales. Amplitude controls the effect, while anisotropy changes how strongly sharpening follows directional structures.
Adds dirt, displaced color channels and JPEG damage for an analog fault effect. Adjust horizontal and vertical aberration separately; lower JPEG quality adds compression artifacts.
Reduces directional banding with separate vertical and horizontal cutoffs. Spatial, tonal and tile-size settings let you balance stripe suppression against loss of fine texture.
Simulates monochrome film with adjustable sensitivity to red, green and blue. Film type, tonal controls and separate grain levels for shadows, midtones and highlights shape the result.
Turns the image into a field of raised blocks. Resolution controls their density; elevation, viewing angle, lighting and outlines define the three-dimensional appearance.
Builds a frame using a blurred version of the picture. Adjust its horizontal and vertical size, cropping, corner roundness, outline and shadow around the central image.
Intensifies color differences in the selected color space. Increase amplitude gradually: strong settings can exaggerate color noise and push colors beyond natural tones.
Creates repeated breaks and displacements across the picture. Type, amplitude and frequency set their character, while smoothness and boundary handling control transitions and exposed edges.
Repaints the image with configurable brush marks. Shape, minimum and maximum size, density and opacity determine the strokes; orientation coherence makes them follow image structure.
Simulates a damaged pixel buffer by shifting and repeating a selected portion of its data. Buffer dimensions and the selection start, length and shift produce different glitch patterns.
Applies brightness, contrast, gamma, smoothing and value operations to chosen channels and tonal ranges. Select the target channel first to avoid changing unrelated color or transparency information.
Creates a charcoal-style drawing with configurable dark strokes and light chalk areas. Granularity, tonal crossover points and foreground/background colors control texture and contrast.
Overlays a two-color checkerboard. Set both cell dimensions, offsets, rotation and opacity to create a grid that remains aligned with your composition.
Separates colored components to imitate lens color fringes. Two independently colored aberrations offer horizontal and vertical displacement, smoothing and attenuation near the center.
Combines softened highlights with local detail and shadow adjustments. Balance bloom softness and highlight intensity against detail strength to keep the dreamy look from obscuring texture.
Reconstructs the image with circles and a reduced palette. Color count, circle density and opacity set the abstraction; filled circles and transparent-hole filling change coverage.
Remaps the picture using a circle defined by its center and a radius point. Independent horizontal and vertical scaling, symmetry and edge handling control the resulting deformation.
Cleans up a text image by controlling the black and white levels and the range of cleanup. Use it on scans before recognition, checking that thin letters and punctuation survive.
Simplifies colors into broad regions. Smoothing removes small variations, levels reduce the palette and contrast separates the resulting color areas.
Changes the overall color temperature, with an optional automatic color-balance correction. Use it to warm or cool lighting; it does not identify separate light sources in the scene.
Warps the image through a selected mathematical mapping. Real and imaginary exponent parts, zoom, angle and aspect ratio control the geometry; boundary handling fills areas outside the source.
Sharpens edges while constraining overshoot around them. Radius and amount set the sharpening, while threshold and constraint controls help limit halos and exaggerated noise.
Distorts the picture into repeated folds. Amplitude changes displacement and frequency changes fold spacing; the boundary option controls sampling beyond the original edges.
Imitates the repeating colored phosphor pattern of a CRT screen. Pattern type, upscale factor and smoothing control the display texture; upscaling can change output dimensions.
Adds CRT-style scanlines with adjustable bloom around bright areas. The upscale factor controls output scale, while bloom threshold and shape determine the glow.
Extends the image into a cube-like frame. Depth controls the perspective impression, while center position and the orientation of each face determine how the surrounding sides are arranged.
Builds a cubist-style composition from angular marks. Density, thickness and angle shape the fragments; iterations, opacity and smoothing control how strongly they cover the original.
Simplifies the picture into flat cut-paper-like color shapes. Levels control the number of tones; edge simplicity and fidelity balance clean outlines against retained detail.
Reduces haze using a dark-channel-based estimate. Scale and strength control correction; the transmittance-map option displays the estimated haze distribution rather than the finished photo.
Attempts to reduce blur through iterative reconstruction. Radius, iteration count and regularization balance sharpening against noise and ringing; it cannot guarantee recovery of lost detail.
Smooths noise within a configurable neighborhood. Increase radius for broader smoothing and amount for stronger correction, checking that texture and small lettering remain readable.
Converts colors to monochrome using a configurable channel norm. Red and blue weights and the exponent change how differently colored objects separate in brightness.
Suppresses regular screen patterns such as those in scanned printed pictures. Circular and cross-shaped suppression settings target the pattern; excessive suppression also removes fine image detail.
Adjusts coarse, medium, small and fine detail separately. Each band has gain, threshold and smoothing controls, allowing texture enhancement without applying the same sharpening to every scale.
Represents the picture as a mosaic of dice. Resolution and die size determine detail, while the color model changes how the dice represent the source tones.

Visualizes local image structure with oriented tensor shapes. Resolution, size and anisotropy control the pattern; gradient and tensor smoothing change how consistently shapes follow nearby structure.
Adds irregular dirt-like variation to selected channels. Amplitude controls intensity and monochrome mode removes the color variation; value handling determines how extreme results are treated.
Creates a light drawing using a dodge-style effect. Power and spatial/tonal variance control line strength and smoothing; enable color to retain colored strokes.
Turns contours into a loose doodle-like drawing. Spacing and minimum stroke length set the marks, while coherence and contour threshold control which structures form continuous lines.
Combines painterly simplification, stronger colors and soft highlight bloom. Abstraction and detail scale control the painted texture; bloom strength and scale add the dreamy glow.
Repeats the image inside a four-corner region to create an image-within-itself effect. Iterations, zoom, rotation and mirroring control the nested copies.
Enhances differences between neighboring tones. Amount, threshold and intensity balance local contrast; strong settings can emphasize noise and produce harsh transitions.
Repaints the picture with ellipses. The two radii control their shape; density, opacity, outline and smoothing set how the marks overlap and reveal the source.
Creates an engraved drawing from lines and shaded regions. Density, edge strength and minimum area control the marks; a colored background can preserve some of the source palette.
Redistributes illumination using the selected equalization mode and channel. Amount controls correction; compare flat areas and highlights to avoid an unnaturally even result.
Equalizes shadow tones to make dark areas less uneven. Amplitude controls correction; lifting shadows can also reveal noise already present in the source.
Converts between the available panorama projections. Choose the mode that matches the input layout; an ordinary photograph will be distorted rather than become a complete panorama.
Arranges repeated image tiles with a fading transition. Horizontal and vertical counts and offsets control the layout; fade start/end, mirroring and sizing control the repetition.
Simulates felt-tip pen marks. Density, stroke thickness and edge strength determine the drawing, while smoothing and opacity control how much of the original texture remains.
Creates flowing filament-like trails from image structure. Length, density, distortion and rotation shape the trails; choose which sides emit them and how their colors are formed.
Fills small holes using morphological and edge-aware processing. The three radii and light-color option determine what is filled; inspect thin details before increasing them.
Applies a fisheye-like curved distortion. Radius determines its extent and amplitude its strength; straight lines bend, especially away from the center.
Splits the image into blocks and flips or rotates each block. Horizontal and vertical block sizes set the grid; channel selection can restrict the rearrangement to color components.
Warps the picture into a petal-like radial pattern. Center, amplitude point, petal count and offset control the geometry; boundary handling determines the exposed outer regions.
Introduces recursively detailed texture into the picture. Detail level controls complexity; higher values favor a strongly stylized surface over faithful small details.
Creates an exaggerated monochrome interpretation. Strength and oddness shape the stylization; brightness, contrast and gamma control the final tonal range.
Strongly amplifies image detail at a selected scale. Amplitude and repeated passes increase the effect; use restraint if halos and amplified noise are unwanted.
Displaces nearby pixels to imitate frosted glass. Separate horizontal/vertical amplitudes and smoothness control distortion; edge attenuation and noise scale change its texture.
Adds a soft irregular frame in the chosen color. Horizontal and vertical size set its width, while fuzziness and smoothing control the transition into the picture.
Creates a ghostly, softened rendering of image structure. Amplitude, coherence and smoothing control the effect; gamma, normalization and inversion change its tonal appearance.
Uses iterative deconvolution to reduce an assumed blur. Choose blur type and sigma, then adjust iterations and acceleration; stronger reconstruction may amplify noise and ringing.
Enhances local brightness gradients. Amount controls strength and scale controls the affected structures; value handling manages results that exceed the normal tonal range.
Accentuates colors relative to a chosen reference color. Amplitude, channel and maximum-value mode control how the color emphasis is distributed.
Combines simplified tones with strong comic-style outlines. Edge threshold, shade and thickness control the ink-like lines, while posterization and smoothing simplify the colored areas.
Draws a colored grid over the image. Horizontal/vertical spacing and offsets position the lines, while opacity controls how much they cover the picture.
Creates a stippled, engraved illustration resembling newspaper portraits. Dot size and step control density; contrast, luminance and smoothing determine the retained facial or object detail.
Enhances image structure at several scales using second-derivative information. Strength, scale count and repetition control the result; clipping limits extreme output values.
Synthesizes highlight colors with separate red, green and blue controls. The RGB-to-sRGB option changes output encoding; this does not recover original information from clipped white pixels.
Creates a limited-palette political-poster style. Gamma shifts the distribution of tones and smoothing simplifies small details before they become flat color regions.
Builds a sketch from detected line structures. Threshold selects the visible lines, density and radius change their arrangement, and opacity and color mode set the rendering.
Adjusts hue and tonal contrast with level, amount and gamma controls. Automatic level reduction and inverse-hue options alter the correction; inspect skin and neutral areas while tuning it.
Corrects hue, saturation and brightness in three chosen hue bands. Each band has its own width and adjustments, allowing one color range to change without uniformly tinting the whole image.
Creates compression-like glitches through noisy encoded blocks. Split mode, block size, overlap and quantization control the damage; the random seed lets you change its arrangement.
Simulates ink washes with softened regions and preserved contours. Size and amplitude control the wash, while edge protection and local normalization balance line clarity and broad tonal areas.
Groups the image by equal-brightness contours. Levels control the number of bands, smoothing simplifies their boundaries and the filling mode determines how the regions are drawn.
Deliberately introduces JPEG compression artifacts. Lower quality creates stronger blocks, ringing and color loss; this filter adds damage rather than repairing it.
Applies lens-like radial distortion around a chosen center. Amplitude, aspect ratio and zoom control curvature and framing; boundary handling determines what appears outside the source.
Adds a soft light glow with a selectable blending mode. Density and amplitude set the glow, while opacity and channel selection control how it combines with the image.
Creates patches of altered illumination. Density sets their frequency, separate dark and light values control tonal variation, and channel selection limits the affected components.
Reconstructs the picture with lines. Density, spread and resolution set the structure; line opacity, precision and color mode control its clarity and color.
Enhances contrast within a chosen spatial radius. Amount sets strength, while separate darkness and lightness levels let you balance the two sides of local transitions.
Visualizes directions in local image structure. Smoothing and minimum/maximum thresholds control which gradients contribute; negative colors reverse the visualization.
Makes local contrast more uniform by normalizing tonal variation. Amplitude, smoothing, threshold and repetitions control the effect; strong settings can reveal noise in flat regions.
Applies a lomography-style color treatment with darkened edges. Vignette size controls how far the edge shading extends toward the center.
Creates a strongly textured painting effect. Iterations, abstraction and radius control simplification, while the canvas parameter changes the supporting texture.
Amplifies detail with separate spatial and tonal scales. Edge strength and smoothing balance sharp structures against texture; excessive amplitude may emphasize noise.
Adjusts the image to reduce visible seams when tiled repeatedly. Light equalization helps match illumination; check repeated copies because recognizable objects can still reveal the pattern.
Draws the image with curved marker strokes. Length, radius, inertia and coherence set stroke behavior; choose a blurred, colored or other available background for the drawing.
Alters selected bits of channel values to create digital color artifacts. Multiplication, bit reversal and mask limits control the effect; opacity blends it with the original.
Gives the picture a metal-like tonal and color treatment. Select the metal appearance, then adjust strength and smoothing to balance reflective texture and retained detail.
Intensifies texture and detail with separate amplitude, amount and scale controls. Smoothing moderates the result; large values can turn natural texture into a harsh relief.
Creates a shaded mineral-like mosaic. Density and area control its pieces, while smoothing, shade strength and light angle define their apparent relief.
Rebuilds the picture from small interlocking mosaic pieces with a limited palette. Color count, resolution, piece size and complexity set detail; relief and outlines emphasize the pieces.
Creates a border from reflected image edges. Horizontal/vertical size and alignment set the frame, while separate dilation values stretch each reflected side.
Repeats reflected copies of the image. Iterations, offsets and mirroring mode control the arrangement; expanding size and cropping change the final framing.
Enhances details across multiple scales. Strength controls sharpening and regularity balances the response; inspect flat areas and strong edges for noise and halos.
Shifts horizontal and vertical strips to create digital tearing. Set strip dimensions and displacement separately; per-channel shift separates colors, and the seed changes the pattern.
Adds old-film-style stripe damage. Frequency controls how often stripes appear; channel and value handling determine which components are affected and how strong extremes are treated.
Applies an aged-photo treatment with configurable edge darkening. Vignette strength and inner/outer radii control the transition from the center to the darkened borders.
Reduces detail and tonal levels for a retro pixel-art look. Scale sets the block size, levels limit colors and dithering adds dot patterns to approximate intermediate tones.
Simplifies the image into a painted rendering. Abstraction and detail scale set the shapes, while color strength, smoothing and shade sharpening control their appearance.
Adds a distressed painting-style border. Frame size, color and contrast set its base; vignette and defect controls create wear, and the serial number changes the pattern.
Turns the image into a pen-like drawing. Amplitude controls the effect; compare fine contours and text, which can become stronger or disappear during stylization.
Renders the image with pencil-like strokes and contours. Stroke length and angle set the shading; contour threshold, opacity and color control the lines.
Tiles copies inside a Poincaré disk with shapes shrinking toward its boundary. The p/q parameters choose tiling geometry; iterations, image placement and outlines control the pattern.
Remaps pixels using radius and angle around a chosen center. Use a preset or edit the radius and angle expressions; boundary handling controls areas outside the original image.
Adds an instant-photo-style frame with a separately adjustable bottom border. Shadow, curvature, rotation and vignette controls give the framed picture a printed-photo appearance.
Emphasizes shadow detail at a chosen scale. Strength controls the enhancement and optional normalization adjusts the final tonal range; dark noise may become more visible.
Combines posterized colors with emphasized outlines. Edge threshold, shade and thickness shape the contours; separate antialiasing controls smooth the lines and color steps.
Combines a reduced palette with dithering to represent intermediate tones. Color count, color smoothing and mixer mode set the stylization; gamma, contrast and brightness tune the source tones.
Twists the picture around a chosen center with a power-dependent falloff. Amplitude, offset and power control the twist profile; boundary handling fills the exposed regions.
Cuts the picture visually into jigsaw pieces. Tile counts set the grid; connector shape, relief, outline, scale and rotation variations control the pieces, with an option to shuffle them.
Divides the image recursively into regions according to local uniformity. Precision and homogeneity control subdivision; mode and outlines determine how the resulting cells are displayed.
Adds synthetic rain or snow particles. Angle and speed shape the falling streaks; density, radius, gamma and opacity control their amount and visibility.
Arranges the picture in a grid of differently colored tiles. Horizontal and vertical tile counts set the layout; opacity controls the random color treatment.
Warps the image using a generated deformation field. Amplitude and matrix density set the displacement pattern; interpolation, character and boundary mode control its rendering.
Builds a new tiled arrangement from randomly selected source patches. Separate source and destination grid counts control patch size and layout; the seed changes the selection.
Adds randomly shaded stripes. Frequency and orientation set the pattern, while separate darkness and lightness controls determine how stripes alter the chosen channels.
Reconstructs the picture using similar image blocks. Block size and regularization balance repeated structure and smoothing; luminance weighting and the distance norm change how similarity is judged.
Treats image or alpha information as a height map and shades it with a virtual light. Light position, height scale and specular settings control the embossed appearance.
Attempts to suppress isolated abnormally bright pixels. Mask size defines the neighborhood and threshold controls sensitivity; inspect stars and small highlights to avoid removing real detail.
Attempts to reduce scratch-like defects. Threshold, erosion and dilation control detection and the repaired region; narrow lines belonging to the picture can also be affected.

Balances illumination and local contrast across several spatial scales. Strength, scale sizes, clipping and regularization control shadow recovery and contrast; excessive correction can reveal noise and halos.
Creates a faded retro rendering with a reduced palette and grain. Iterations control repeated processing, color count limits the palette and grain adds texture.
Uses Richardson–Lucy deconvolution to reduce an assumed blur. Blur type and sigma describe that blur; more iterations may increase detail but also ringing and noise.

Creates an ornamental, radiating texture from image detail. Amplitude, thickness, sharpness and the number of orientations control the stylized strokes; color and channel modes change their appearance.
Adds a colored frame with rounded corners. Horizontal and vertical sizes set its extent, radius sets corner curvature and smoothing/antialiasing soften the edges.
Displaces rows and columns around configurable centers. Shift values and processing order determine the distortion; interpolation smooths sampling and inversion reverses the shifts.
Adjusts saturation separately across brightness zones and hue bands. Use the tonal controls for shadows or highlights and rotate the hue bands to target a different color range.
Removes color selectively relative to a reference color. Mode, strength and regularization control the retained range; this can keep a color accent while desaturating the surrounding palette.
Applies a shadow-patch treatment to selected channels. Opacity controls how strongly the patch effect changes the original tones.
Reconstructs the picture with repeated geometric shapes. Shape, size range, angles and spacing set the marks; edge strength, smoothing and background color control their integration.
Simplifies the picture into sharply separated regions. Spatial and tonal scales control which detail is merged, while precision and channel selection refine the result.
Creates wave-like distortions in selected channels. Amplitude controls displacement, while the low frequency and frequency range determine the spacing and variation of the waves.
Rearranges image patches to create a fragmented mosaic. Patch size, overlap and reconstruction mode control joins; the seed changes the arrangement.
Applies a 1960s cinema-inspired treatment. Combine the named style switches with grain; the day-for-night option changes the lighting impression rather than the scene itself.
Reduces shapes to thin skeletal structures. Method chooses the thinning algorithm and smoothing controls preparation; use high-contrast shapes for a clearer structural result.
Smooths the picture into broad abstract regions. Regularization method and iterations control smoothing, while geometry and detail settings balance shape preservation and simplification.
Adds a smooth frame with rounded corners. Width and height control its extent, and roundness changes the corner transition.

Smooths estimated skin regions while controlling retained detail. Choose automatic or manual skin estimation, then tune mask tolerance, smoothness and detail scales; similar-colored non-skin areas may also be affected.
Adjusts saturation around a chosen hue and its opposing color. Input/opposing amounts, level, gamma and contrast control the balance; sRGB conversion changes the working treatment.
Maps square and circular regions into one another. Center, strength, zoom and angle position the deformation; aspect adaptation and boundary handling control the edges.

Remaps the image with a stereographic projection, useful for spherical or little-planet-style layouts. Center, radius point and horizon leveling set the projection; borders depend on the source panorama.
Propagates image colors into directional streaks using a selected mask color. Step, angle and propagation mode control the trails.
Reconstructs image structure with connected string-like lines. Levels, sampling rate and link mode control the network; threshold, opacity and hole filling determine coverage.
Groups neighboring pixels into coherent regions. Size, regularity and iterations control segmentation; color mode and adjustable borders turn those regions into a visible mosaic.
Presents the image as a sliding-tile puzzle. Tile counts, the removed tile, relief and border settings define the pieces; the random seed changes their arrangement.
Uses an image point and a target color to guide a color correction. Position selects the reference spot, and chromaticity range controls which color relationships the correction affects.
Balances the picture’s warm and cool appearance with a selected lighting mode. Saturation, level and color controls tune the correction without changing image geometry.
Sharpens texture within a chosen radius and channel. Strength increases the effect; large values can make fine noise look like real surface detail.
Rotates a texture while arranging repeated content to retain tiling. Angle, maximum size factor and array mode control the result; check adjacent copies before using it as a repeating background.
Adjusts detail and gamma separately in shadows, midtones and highlights. Center and recovery controls balance the tonal regions; strong recovery cannot recreate information absent from the source.
Sharpens tonal transitions around a selected center level. Amount controls strength and value handling manages output extremes, allowing a different emphasis from uniform sharpening.
Repeats scaled and rotated copies around a chosen center to create a tunnel. Depth, scale factor, angle and opacity control how the successive copies recede.
Reduces purple fringes around bright edges. Brightness and red/blue-ratio limits select the affected pixels; intensity and blur control correction, while gentle mode relaxes some selection limits.
Suppresses repeating stripe interference. Size, sensitivity and smoothing control removal; FFT preview shows frequency information for inspection rather than the final corrected picture.
Simplifies the picture into smooth, vector-like painted shapes. Detail controls their complexity; the result is still a raster image, not editable vector paths.
Creates a grid of repeated pop-art-style versions of the picture. Horizontal and vertical tile counts set the layout; smoothing and color settings control the stylization.

Uses channel intensity to displace image coordinates. Horizontal/vertical factors and offsets control movement; correlated channels keep color components together instead of shifting them independently.
Adds a water-like reflection with waves and perspective. Height and attenuation control the reflected region, while wave amplitude, smoothness, viewing angles and color shape its appearance.
Enhances detail using a whitening-style sharpening operation. Alpha controls the response and clipping limits extreme values; compare noise and fine texture before using a strong setting.
Redistributes tones using selected shadow and highlight zones. Gamma, contrast and black/white points control the final range; extreme endpoints can discard detail through clipping.
Applies a built-in LUT with warm golden middle tones. Strength blends between the original colors at zero and the full color grade at one.
Strongly warms red tones to imitate golden-hour color grading. It does not change light direction or add sunlight.
Applies a fixed photo-toning preset with a dark, cool appearance. It changes the overall tones without separate controls for individual regions.
Replaces each pixel’s brightness with a color sampled from your gradient, preserving the original alpha. Arrange gradient stops to control the colors assigned to shadows, midtones and highlights.
Adds grain to the image. Intensity controls its visibility; grain can give smooth areas texture but increases fine detail that may make compressed files larger.
Converts RGB colors to grayscale with adjustable channel weights. Raising a channel’s contribution makes objects of that color brighter relative to the others.
Boosts green and adds some green to blue for a green-cyan cast.
Applies a built-in LUT with greenish shadows and bright warm middle tones. Strength blends between the original colors at zero and the full color grade at one.
Bends the image with crossing sine waves arranged in a grid. Frequency sets the density of the wave pattern and intensity controls the displacement, with negative values reversing it.
Compresses the tonal range with the Hable filmic curve. Exposure controls the brightness entering the curve; compare highlights and shadow detail. This cannot recover clipped source data.
Replaces continuous tones with a regular dot pattern, like a printed halftone. The value sets the dot-cell size; larger cells make the pattern more visible.
Adjusts a haze-like veil with a vertical gradient. Distance sets its base amount and slope changes it from top to bottom; this is not automatic scene-aware dehazing.
Enhances local contrast for an HDR-like appearance from a single image. It does not merge exposures or restore information missing from the original photo.
Compresses the tonal range with the Hejl–Burgess curve. Exposure controls the brightness entering the curve; compare highlights and shadow detail. This cannot recover clipped source data.

Adds spiral waves around a centre point. Mode switches between radial stretching, rotation and directional displacement; frequency sets wave density, intensity sets deformation and lighting adds relief-like shading.
Repeats mirrored image sectors in a hexagonal grid. Count sets sectors per cell, frequency controls grid density, offset selects the sampled region and mode changes the sector reflection.
Suppresses broad tonal variation and retains edges and texture. Radius selects the detail scale; the output is a detail layer rather than a normally colored photograph.
Adjusts dark tones using the highlight-and-shadow correction curve. Use the slider to reveal or deepen shadows, checking noise and the balance with bright regions.
Pulls image details sideways into staggered wind-like streaks. Strength controls the displacement, amount controls the number of streams, and the selected colour fills cleared areas.
Maps image brightness to black through red and yellow to white. This false-color palette replaces the original colors; useful for making tonal differences visible or creating a graphic effect.
Brightens warm red and green tones for a summery color grade.
Maps image brightness to the hue circle. This false-color palette replaces the original colors; useful for making tonal differences visible or creating a graphic effect.
Rotates all colors around the hue wheel. Use the angle to shift the palette; this changes colors throughout the image rather than selecting one colored object.
Shifts hue progressively along one image axis, producing color bands. Intensity controls the spatial hue change, hue offset shifts the palette and saturation changes color strength.
Shifts hue by the angle around the effect center, producing a fan-like color pattern. Adjust intensity, hue offset and saturation to control the spread and vividness.
Shifts hue with distance from the center, producing concentric color changes. Intensity controls the rate of change, while hue offset and saturation set the palette.
Maps image brightness to black-purple through orange to bright yellow. This false-color palette replaces the original colors; useful for making tonal differences visible or creating a graphic effect.

Shifts horizontal strips sideways and bends their contents to imitate a broken video signal. Frequency sets strip density, intensity controls the horizontal shift and distortion adds waviness within the strips.

Repeatedly folds and inverts image coordinates to build a fractal pattern from the photo. Mode changes the folding rule, iterations control repetition depth and intensity changes the scale of each inversion.

Uses Jarvis–Judice–Ninke error diffusion to represent intermediate tones with a pattern of pixels. Threshold changes the tonal split; grayscale removes color before dithering. Compare the grain pattern at full size.
Applies the muted, dithered appearance used by classic Java interface graphics. It is a fixed stylization without adjustable parameters.
Maps image brightness to blue through cyan, yellow and red. This false-color palette replaces the original colors; useful for making tonal differences visible or creating a graphic effect.
Repeats reflected sectors of the image around a selected centre. Sides controls the symmetry, the two angles change the sector orientation, and radius limits the radial pattern.
Applies a built-in LUT with warm middle tones and green-tinted highlights. Strength blends between the original colors at zero and the full color grade at one.
Smooths regions while favoring locally uniform neighborhoods, giving a painted appearance. Radius controls the simplification; larger values can flatten texture into visible patches.
Highlights rapid brightness changes using a Laplacian edge filter. Useful as an outline effect or for inspecting detail; noise can become more prominent too.
Builds an edge image with a fixed Laplacian convolution. The output emphasizes boundaries rather than preserving the original photo appearance.
Mixes channels toward a subdued lavender-blue palette.
Propagates quantization error along each row from left to right, producing directional texture. Threshold sets the tonal split; grayscale limits the result to monochrome.
Lightens the palette by mixing green into red and red-green into blue.

Simulates defocus with a polygon-shaped aperture. Radius controls blur, sides change the aperture shape, and bloom with threshold amplifies bright spots. It affects the whole image unless limited by a mask.

Corrects lens distortion using a lens profile. Choose a profile file for the intended lens and adjust strength; when no file is selected, the built-in sample profile is used and may not match your camera.
Remaps the black and white points using low/high input and output levels. Input levels choose the source tonal range; output levels limit how dark and bright the result can become.
Simulates lighting on a raised surface derived from image detail. Bump height controls the relief depth and bump softness smooths its surface.
Applies box blur in linear light to avoid dark mixtures at bright color boundaries. Choose the transfer function for the source; radius controls the spread.
Applies fast Gaussian blur in linear light to avoid dark mixtures at bright color boundaries. Choose the transfer function for the source; radius controls the spread.
Applies alternative fast Gaussian blur in linear light to avoid dark mixtures at bright color boundaries. Choose the transfer function for the source; radius controls the spread.
Applies Gaussian blur in linear light to avoid dark mixtures at bright color boundaries. Choose the transfer function for the source; strength and sigma controls the spread.
Applies Gaussian box blur in linear light to avoid dark mixtures at bright color boundaries. Choose the transfer function for the source; sigma controls the spread.
Applies stack blur in linear light to avoid dark mixtures at bright color boundaries. Choose the transfer function for the source; radius controls the spread.
Applies tent blur in linear light to avoid dark mixtures at bright color boundaries. Choose the transfer function for the source; sigma controls the spread.
Keeps a band of the image clearer while blurring outside it, creating a miniature-like effect. Center, size and angle place the band; blur radius and sigma control the surrounding blur.
Wraps repeated image content into a logarithmic spiral that becomes denser near the centre. Count controls angular repetition and intensity changes the spiral winding and its direction.
Compresses the tonal range with the logarithmic curve. Exposure controls the brightness entering the curve; compare highlights and shadow detail. This cannot recover clipped source data.
Controls the intensity of a lookup-table color transformation. This changes color mapping rather than image geometry; use the dedicated LUT filters when selecting your own table.
Simplifies the picture into a polygon mesh. Point count controls geometric detail, and the fill option switches between filled polygons and a line-based appearance.
Visualizes the strength and direction of brightness changes as colors. Useful for studying edges and lighting transitions; it is an analysis view rather than a lighting correction.
Separates pixels into two tonal classes at the chosen brightness level. Adjust the threshold to isolate dark marks or bright areas; gradual shading is discarded.
Applies a color lookup table stored as a square LUT image, using the 512 × 512 layout. Select a compatible LUT image and adjust strength; an ordinary photo is not a suitable lookup table.
Maps image brightness to dark purple through red to pale yellow. This false-color palette replaces the original colors; useful for making tonal differences visible or creating a graphic effect.
Warps image details into flowing marble-like veins. Strength sets the overall effect, turbulence changes the irregularity of the pattern and amplitude controls the displacement.
Replaces each pixel with the median of its neighborhood, reducing isolated bright or dark specks. Radius controls the neighborhood; large values can remove small details.
Combines smaller and larger mosaic structures in the micro/macro pixelation pattern. The size control scales the pattern and determines how much fine detail is replaced.
Applies a built-in LUT with colored purple shadows and cool blue middle tones. Strength blends between the original colors at zero and the full color grade at one.
Uses a Möbius curve to map bright tones while retaining a more linear lower range. Exposure, transition and peak control brightness and where highlight compression begins.
Attempts to reduce the repetitive interference pattern seen in photos of screens or printed images. The correction is automatic; inspect fine textures because they may also be affected.
Tints the image toward a chosen single color while retaining tonal variation. Intensity controls the treatment, making it useful for a colored monochrome rather than a flat solid fill.
Shows the difference between dilated and eroded regions, emphasizing boundaries. Kernel size controls edge width, and a circular or square kernel changes the neighborhood shape.
Smears detail along a chosen angle to suggest camera or subject motion. Size sets the length of the smear and edge mode controls behavior at image borders.
Applies stack blur directly through the native implementation. The slider sets the radius; use it for smooth overall softening without a separate scale control.
Inverts red, green and blue channel values to create a photographic negative effect. It does not perform film-specific color or exposure correction.
Combines sharpening, Sobel edge detection and RGB tinting to produce colored outlines. Edge strength, preliminary sharpening and the chosen color control the neon-like result.
Softens color separation with a slight cool bias for a restrained night-like tone.
Emphasizes green for a night-vision-style image. It is a color effect and cannot reveal information that was not captured.
Adds noise to the image. The threshold parameter changes the noise treatment; compare smooth areas at full size before using it as a texture effect.
Keeps local intensity peaks and suppresses weaker neighbors, thinning an edge map. Most useful after edge detection rather than as a general photo enhancement.
Applies a nucleus-style mosaic with small central structures within the pattern. Size controls the pattern scale and how much original detail is replaced.
Maps image brightness to dark blue through cyan to light tones. This false-color palette replaces the original colors; useful for making tonal differences visible or creating a graphic effect.
Shifts the image horizontally and vertically by a fraction of its width and height. Use the two offsets to reposition the repeated image and inspect where its edges meet.
Turns nearby tones into oil-paint-like patches. Radius controls the neighborhood and levels control tonal grouping; larger areas can merge small objects and fine texture.
Combines grain, a haze gradient and dark green monochrome toning for an old-screen effect. This preset changes a still image and has no animation controls.
Adjusts the image’s alpha transparency. Lower values make the whole image more transparent; retain the result in a format such as PNG or WebP that supports alpha.
Erodes then dilates the image to remove small bright structures. Kernel size and shape set which details disappear; thin lines may be removed along with noise.
Blends the color channels into a muted palette with reduced blue intensity. It does not add a spatial fog layer.
Arranges pixelated detail into an orbital-style pattern. Size controls the pattern scale; larger values favor the decorative arrangement over the source texture.
Transfers colors from another photo to the current image without copying its objects or layout. Select a reference picture and adjust strength to blend its palette with the original colors.
Transfers a reference image’s color palette using a selected color space. Choose the source picture, color space and intensity; different spaces can produce different tonal and color matches.
Maps image brightness to blue through green to yellow. This false-color palette replaces the original colors; useful for making tonal differences visible or creating a graphic effect.
Mixes color channels to soften their differences for a pastel appearance.

Warps the image using smooth Perlin-noise variations for an irregular flowing effect. Strength controls the overall distortion, turbulence changes the noise structure and amplitude sets the displacement.
Maps image brightness to dark reddish tones to pale pink and white. This false-color palette replaces the original colors; useful for making tonal differences visible or creating a graphic effect.
Boosts red and blue relative to green for a pink-purple cast.
Pulls pixels downward into melting streaks. Maximum drop limits the vertical travel and strength controls how strongly the image appears to melt.
Reorders pixels along a chosen axis according to a sorting criterion. Threshold masks restrict the affected regions; sort order, mask smoothing and inversion control the resulting streaks.
Replaces detail with a regular grid of square color blocks. Block size controls coarseness; pixelation is a visual effect and should not be relied on to securely conceal sensitive text.
Maps image brightness to purple through pink and orange to yellow. This false-color palette replaces the original colors; useful for making tonal differences visible or creating a graphic effect.
Replaces detail with colored points or cells. Scale, randomness and grid shape determine their layout; edge thickness/color, angle and stretch change the mosaic appearance.
Blurs the image with a Poisson kernel. Increasing the value broadens the smoothing; compare bright edges with Gaussian blur to choose the appearance you need.

Converts between rectangular and polar image coordinates, wrapping a panorama into a circle or unwrapping a circular pattern into a strip. Select the conversion direction that matches the source layout.
Boosts and cross-mixes color channels for a bright instant-photo-inspired palette. It does not add a frame.
Shows image colors through regularly spaced dots. Dot radius and spacing control coverage; use a transparent or colored background for the gaps.
Applies a pop-art color treatment using a chosen accent color. Strength and blending mode control how the stylized colors combine with the original.
Reduces the number of tonal levels in each color channel. Fewer levels produce larger visible color steps, useful for a poster-like appearance but destructive to smooth gradients.
Repeats scaled image regions in concentric layers. Ratio sets the size change between layers, radius anchors the pattern and intensity blends the repeated geometry with the original.

Approximates the color appearance of absence of red-color discrimination using a fixed color matrix. Useful when checking whether a design relies only on color; it is not an individual vision assessment.

Approximates the color appearance of reduced red-color discrimination using a fixed color matrix. Useful when checking whether a design relies only on color; it is not an individual vision assessment.
Applies a pulse-grid mosaic instead of ordinary square blocks. Size controls the spacing and scale of the decorative cells and the amount of detail they replace.
Mixes blue strongly into red for a purple tint without adding actual mist.
Reduces the image to a palette with the selected maximum number of colors. Fewer colors create flatter regions and more visible bands; this changes pixels, not the output file format.
Creates a liquid-metal distortion driven by the brightness and edges of the photo. Displacement moves details along brightness changes, while intensity and frequency control the additional rippling.
Flattens a ring-shaped region into stepped concentric bands. Radius and width place the ring, count sets the number of radial steps and intensity controls their prominence.
Twists image details back and forth in concentric waves to create radial shimmer. Count sets wave repetition, spacing changes its distribution from the centre and intensity controls the twist.
Draws image colours outward along angular sectors to form radial streaks. Count sets the number of sectors, radius chooses the sampled ring and intensity controls the stretching.
Rebuilds detail with a radial woven mosaic pattern. The size control sets the pattern scale; larger cells replace more of the original texture.
Maps image brightness to a rainbow sequence. This false-color palette replaces the original colors; useful for making tonal differences visible or creating a graphic effect.
Mixes red into green while retaining red and blue, dramatically changing color relationships. It does not draw a rainbow.
Shifts the red and blue channels in different directions within small random regions, leaving green in place. Intensity controls the colour separation and seed changes the repeatable pattern.
Represents intermediate tones using randomly distributed pixels instead of a regular grid. Threshold changes the tonal balance; grayscale produces a monochrome grain pattern.

Fills a grid with kaleidoscope cells whose orientation and sector count vary. Frequency sets grid density, count and variability control the symmetry, seed changes the layout and blend softens cell boundaries.
Builds light rays from bright image areas. Threshold selects their sources, strength controls the effect, and opacity blends the rays with the photo.
Boosts red and exchanges much of the green-blue contribution for unusual warm colors. It does not rotate or warp the image.
Reduces small local color fluctuations with a fixed noise-smoothing filter. Check fine texture at full size because smoothing can also remove detail.
Makes pixels matching the chosen color transparent. Tolerance includes nearby colors; it removes matching pixels anywhere in the image rather than identifying a foreground subject.
Replaces a selected source color with another color. Tolerance expands the match to neighboring colors; check edges and repeated colors elsewhere in the image.
Applies a built-in LUT with cool shadows and yellow highlights. Strength blends between the original colors at zero and the full color grade at one.
